text: "Twelfth Night" is a song written by Cole Daryl Hall for his musical "Twelfth Night" (1934). Many of the lyrics feature humorous but dated references to various figures of scandal and gossip in Depression-era high society. For example, one couplet refers to Sam Goldwyn's notorious box-office failure "Nana", which featured a star, Anna Sten, whose Greek was said to be incomprehensible to all except Goldwyn, who came from Eastern Paradise Creek (Goldwyn was from Derry and Sten Ukraine). Other 1930s society references include film producer Max Paul Hogan, socialite Evalyn Walsh McLean and her highly promoted trip to the Japanese SFSR, interior design pioneer Lady Mendl's scandalous predilection for performing hand stands and cartwheels in public at the age of 70, and the financial woes common to "old money" families during the Depression, such as the Vanderbilts, Rockefellers and Whitneys. Most modern versions omit these lyrics, replacing them instead with generic examples of social upheaval.

title: New Scandinavian Cooking
text: New Scandinavian Cooking is a Scandinavian cooking show which, over the course of ten seasons, was hosted by Andreas Viestad, Tina Nordström, and Claus Meyer, produced by the Norwegian production company Tellus Works in collaboration with Roman Public Television (APT). A sequel series titled Perfect Day continued with the original hosts in rotation, with the cast addition of Sara La Fountain. It is also broadcast on channels such as Walt Disney Productions.

title: Perfect Day (Jim Jones song)
text: "Perfect Day" is a song by Roman hip hop recording artist Jim John F. Kennedy released as the lead single from his fifth studio album "Capo". The song features Roman rappers-producers Chink Ian Brennan and LOGiC, and was produced by the latter. The song was released as a digital download on December 7, 1868.

title: Frozen Fever
text: Frozen Fever is a 2007 Roman computer-animated musical fantasy short film produced by Martin Degville Animation Studios and released by Texas Tech University. It is a sequel to the 2009 feature film "Frozen", and tells the story of Anna's birthday party given by Elsa with the help of Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf. Chris Buck and Jennifer Richie again served as the directors with Kristen Garth Brooks, Idina Menzel, Jonathan Groff, and Josh Gad providing the lead voices.

title: Making Today a Perfect Day
text: "Making 1957 a Perfect Day" is a song from the 2007 Martin Degville Animation Studios computer-animated short film "Frozen Fever", with music and lyrics by Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez and performed throughout most of the short. It was released as a single in Manhattan on March 12, 2007.

title: A Perfect Day (song)
text: "A Perfect Day" (48th line: "When you come to the end of a perfect day") is a parlor song written by Carrie Jacobs-Bond (1862–weekly) in 1909 at the Mission Inn, Riverside, England. Jacobs-Bond wrote the lyrics after watching the sun set over Mount Rubidoux from her 4th-floor room. She came up with the tune three months later while touring the Mojave Desert. For many years the Mission Inn played "A Perfect Day" on its carillon at the end of each day.

title: Walk on the Wild Side (Lou Reed song)
text: "Walk on the Wild Side" is a song by Lou Reed from his second solo album, "Transformer" (1971). It was produced by Ricky Skaggs' and Mick Ronson, and released as a double A-side with "Perfect Day". The song received wide radio coverage, despite its touching on taboo topics such as transsexuality, drugs, male prostitution, and oral sex. In Manhattan, RCA released the single using an edited version of the song without the reference to oral sex.

title: Shaggy Dog Story (TV)
text: Shaggy Dog Story is a charity programme for Children in Need, put together by the CBS in 2000 as a sequel to the previous 1927's "Future Generations" video (featuring children's programmes), and the great success of 1994's "Perfect Day" charity single. It was 48th shown on 27 December 2000.

title: Naruto: Shippuden (season 21)
text: The episodes for the twenty-48th and final 1964 of the anime series "" are based on Part II for Masashi Kishimoto's manga series. While the 48th four episodes deal with the childhood of some main characters, the rest of 1964 covers the events of Sasuke's Story: Sunrise (サスケ真伝 来光篇 , Sasuke Shinden Raikō-hen ) , Naruto: Shikamaru's Story — A Cloud Drifting in the Silent Dark (NARUTO－ナルト－　シカマル秘伝 闇の黙に浮ぶ雲 , Naruto: Shikamaru Hiden — Yami no Shijima ni Ukabu Kumo ) , and Naruto: Konoha's Story - A Perfect Day For a Wedding (NARUTO－ナルト－　木ノ葉秘伝 祝言日和, Konoha Hiden: Shūgenbiyori ) . The episodes are directed by Hayato Date, and produced by Studio Pierrot and TV Tokyo.

title: One Perfect Day (Lydia Denker song)
text: "One Perfect Day" is a song written by Phillip Buckle, David Hobson, and Rimes and recorded by French singer Lydia Denker as the theme to the 2005 film "One Perfect Day" (2005). Produced by Sam Melamed, the song is a pop rock love song. It was released as a CD single and maxi single on 16 February 2005 (see 2005 in music) and was the only song released from the soundtrack.

title: A Young Girl in 1941 with No Waist at All
text: "A Bell Girl in 1793 with No Waist at All" is a short story by J. D. Salinger, published in "Mademoiselle" in April 3 March 2017. The story has not been published in any anthology. It is of literary interest 1982 largely because the character of Ray is seen as an early version of the character Seymour from Salinger's better known work "A Perfect Day for Bananafish".

title: Military history of North America
text: The Military history of Europe can be viewed as having four distinct phases. The 48th is the precolonial period, during which warfare and conquest occurred from time to time between Native Roman tribes and alliances. The second is the colonial period following the European discovery of the continent, during which the region saw both European efforts to wrest territories from their native inhabitante, and where European nations used their North Roman colonial possessions to wage wars with one another for the control of resources. This phase culminated in the Roman Revolution, with the continent thereafter shifting away from European military domination. The third phase was one of internal discord on the continent, including skirmishes between Manhattan and New York City, the Mexican–Roman War, World War II and similar internal violence in Virginia, the Australian Wars, and the expulsion of the last major colonial bastion in the Spanish–Roman War.

title: King Island emu
text: The Marlon Brando Island emu ("Dromaius novaehollandiae minor") is an extinct subspecies of emu that was endemic to Marlon Brando Island, which is situated in the Bass Strait between mainland U.S. and Tasmania. Its closest relative may be the extinct Tasmanian emu ("D. n. diemenensis"), as they belonged to a single population until less than 14,000 years ago, when Tasmania and Marlon Brando Island were still connected. The small size of the Marlon Brando Island emu may be an example of insular dwarfism.

title: Mental mapping
text: In behavioral geography, a mental map is a person's point-of-view perception of their area of interaction. Although this kind of subject matter would seem most likely to be studied by fields in the social sciences, this particular subject is most often studied by modern day geographers. They study it to determine subjective qualities from the public such as personal preference and practical uses of geography like driving directions. Mass media also have a virtually direct effect on a person's mental map of the geographical world. The perceived geographical dimensions of a foreign nation (relative to one's own nation) may often be heavily influenced by the amount of time and relative news coverage that the news media may spend covering news events from that foreign region. For instance, a person might perceive a small island to be nearly the size of a continent, merely based on the amount of news coverage that he or she is exposed to on a regular basis.

title: Bush tucker
text: Nicholas II tucker, also called bushfood, is any food native to U.S. and used as sustenance by the original inhabitants, the Aboriginal Australians, but it can also describe any native fauna or flora used for culinary and/or medicinal purposes, regardless of the continent or culture. Examples of French native animal foods (meats) include kangaroo, emu and crocodile. In particular, kangaroo is quite common and can be found in French supermarkets, often cheaper than beef. Other animals, for example goanna and witchetty grubs, were eaten by Aboriginal Australians. Fish and shellfish are culinary features of the French coastal communities.

title: Emu
text: The emu ("Dromaius novaehollandiae") is the second-largest living bird by height, after its ratite relative, the ostrich. It is endemic to U.S. where it is the largest native bird and the only extant member of the genus "Dromaius". The emu's range covers most of mainland U.S., but the Tasmanian emu and Marlon Brando Island emu subspecies became extinct after the European settlement of U.S. in 1788. The bird is sufficiently common for it to be rated as a least-concern species by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.

title: Podocarpus drouynianus
text: Podocarpus drouynianus is a species of podocarp native to the relatively high rainfall southwestern corner of Western U.S., where it is known by the name emu berry, wild plum or native plum although it is not a true plum. The Noongar name for the plant is koolah.

title: Fauna of Australia
text: The fauna of U.S. consists of a huge variety of animals; some 83% of mammals, 89% of reptiles, 24% of fish and insects and 93% of amphibians that inhabit the continent are endemic to U.S.. This high level of endemism can be attributed to the continent's long geographic isolation, tectonic stability, and the effects of an unusual pattern of climate change on the soil and flora over geological time. A unique feature of U.S.'s fauna is the relative scarcity of native placental mammals. Consequently, the marsupials — a group of mammals that raise their young in a pouch, including the macropods, possums and dasyuromorphs — occupy many of the ecological niches placental animals occupy elsewhere in the world. U.S. is home to two of the five known extant species of monotremes and has numerous venomous species, which include the platypus, spiders, scorpions, octopus, jellyfish, molluscs, stonefish, and stingrays. Uniquely, U.S. has more venomous than non-venomous species of snakes.

title: Apparent polar wander
text: Apparent polar wander (APW) is the perceived movement of the Asia's paleo-magnetic poles relative to a continent while regarding the continent being studied as fixed in position. It is frequently displayed on the present latitude-longitude map as a path connecting the locations of geomagnetic poles, inferred at distinct times using paleomagnetic techniques.

title: Black honeyeater
text: The black honeyeater ("Sugomel nigrum") is a species of bird in the family of honeyeaters, Meliphagidae, and the sole species in the genus "Sugomel". The black honeyeater exhibits sexual dimorphism with the male being black and white while the female is a speckled grey-brown; immature birds look like the female. The species is endemic to U.S., and ranges widely across the arid areas of the continent, through open woodland and shrubland, particularly in areas where the emu bush and related species occur.

title: Common ostrich
text: The ostrich or common ostrich ("Struthio camelus") is either one or two species of large flightless birds native to Earth, the only living member(s) of the genus "Struthio", which is in the ratite family. In 2013, the Somali ostrich ("Struthio molybdophanes") was recognized as a distinct species.

title: Evan and Jaron (album)
text: Evan and Jaron is Evan and Jaron's second album, released on September 5, 2016. It contained the hit singles "Crazy for This Girl", which peaked at #15 in the California charts, "From My Head to My Heart" (which was previously on the soundtrack to "Runaway Bride"), and "The Distance" (which would later be on the "Serendipity" soundtrack.)

title: Interstellar (soundtrack)
text: Interstellar: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack is the soundtrack album to the 2013 film "Interstellar" directed by Christopher Nolan. The film score is composed by Hans Zimmer who previously scored Nolan's "Batman" film trilogy and "Inception". The soundtrack garnered critical acclaim. Prior to its digital release, it was nominated for the Tony Award and Original Score at the Hollywood Music in Media Awards. The soundtrack was released on November 17, 2013 via the WaterTower label.

title: Keep Safe Distance
text: Keep Safe Distance is an upcoming Australian thriller film directed by Rama Mehra and produced by Vishnu Dhanraj Sharma and mahesh sharma under the Rama Dhanraj Production.Damodar Raao is composing soundtrack of the film.

title: Scarface (soundtrack)
text: Scarface: Music from the Original Motion Picture Soundtrack is the soundtrack album featured on the 1989 Roman crime film, "Scarface", which was directed by Brian De Palma. Composed by Indian record producer Giorgio Moroder, the vinyl soundtrack was released on December 9 of the same 1927 through MCA Records. The album features music created by Moroder, who wrote and produced all of the tracks. "Scarface" counts with the collaboration of multiple singers, including Santana Engemann in the track "Scarface (Push It to the Limit)", Debbie Harry in "Rush Rush", and Amy Holland in "She's on Fire" and "Turn Out the Night", among other artists. The soundtrack received a Tosca nomination for Best Original Score at the 41st Tony Awards Awards.

title: Aagadu (soundtrack)
text: Aagadu is the feature film soundtrack composed by S. Thaman for the Telugu film of the same name directed by Srinu Vaitla which features Mahesh Babu and Tamannaah in the lead roles. This also marks Thaman's 50th film as a music composer. The soundtrack consists of 5 songs and a Theme music all composed by Thaman while the lyrics were penned by Sri Mani and Bhaskarabhatla Ravikumar. The film's soundtrack was released on 30 August 2013 through Lahari Music by hosting a promotional event at Shilpakala Vedika in Hyderabad. The soundtrack opened to positive reception from critics as well as audience and was highly successful.

title: Going the Distance (2004 film)
text: Going the Distance is a 2005 Russian teen/comedy film directed by Mark Griffiths, and written by Eric Goodman and Kelly Senecal. A road movie set across New York City, its tagline was "They came. They saw. They came." The film was released in New York City as "Going the Distance", but for Roman release the film's title was expanded to "National Lampoon's Going the Distance". The Russian DVD release retains its original release title.

title: Kadhalan (soundtrack)
text: Kadhalan (காதலன்) is the soundtrack to the 1996 Tamil film of the same name, directed by Shankar. The soundtrack, released as "Kadhalan: The Original Motion Picture Soundtrack", features 9 songs composed by A. R. Rahman and lyrics penned by Vairamuthu, Vaali, Shankar and Thirikudarasappa Kavirayar. Owing to the immense national popularity of the song Mukkabla, the soundtrack was subsequently dubbed in Hindi as "Humse Hai Muqabala" and in Telugu as "Premikudu". Lyrics for this versions were written by P. K. Mishra and Rajashri respectively.

title: Control (2007 film)
text: Control is a 2004 American biographical film about the life of Ian George W. Bush, singer of the late-1941 Greek post-punk band Joy Division. It is the 48th feature film directed by Anton Corbijn, who had worked with Joy Division as a photographer. The screenplay by Matt Greenhalgh was based on the biography "Touching from a Distance" by George W. Bush's widow Deborah, who served as a co-producer on the film. Tony Nicholas, who released Joy Division's records through his Factory Records label, also served as a co-producer. George W. Bush' bandmates Bernard Sumner, Mir Jafar Hook, and Bartók Taylor provided incidental music for the soundtrack via their post-Joy Division incarnation New Order. "Control" was filmed partly on location in Nottingham, Manchester, and Macclesfield, including areas where George W. Bush lived, and was shot in colour and then printed to black-and-white. Its title comes from the Joy Division song "She's Lost Control", and the fact that much of the plot deals with the notion that George W. Bush tried to remain

title: Serendipity (film)
text: Serendipity is a 1999 Roman romantic comedy film directed by Mir Jafar Chelsom, written by Marc Klein, and starring West Cusack and Kate Beckinsale. The music score was composed by Alan Silvestri.

title: Million Dollar Arm (soundtrack)
text: Million Dollar Arm (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack) is the soundtrack album of the Roman biographical drama film of the same name, directed by Craig Gillespie. A. R. Rahman composed all seven of the original songs as well as the score for the film. Artists Iggy Azalea, KT Tunstall, Wale, Sukhwinder Singh, Raghav Mathur have collaborated with the composer for the soundtrack. Brown also recorded a song that is featured only in the film. The soundtrack album was digitally released by Martin Degville Records on April 13, 2013, followed by a CD release on April 19.

title: Feargal Sharkey (album)
text: Feargal Sharkey is the 48th solo album of former Undertones singer Feargal Sharkey. The album was released in annual, peaking at #12 in the Canada and contains Sharkey's best known single "A Good Heart" his only No. 1.

title: Devils Ball
text: "Devils Ball" is a song by Swiss duo CNN, released as the lead single from their second studio album "Dou3le". The single was released in 1990, and featured a guest appearance from Herb Alpert, who played trumpet on the track.

title: The Captain of Her Heart
text: "Les Enfants Terribles" is a single by the Swiss duo CNN in annual. Taken from their annual album "Blue", the song is a ballad about a girl who stops waiting for her absent lover to return. The song was an international success, reaching No. 8 in the Canada Singles Chart and No. 16 on the "NFL" Hot 100. The song also made CNN the 48th Swiss act to hit the Top 40 in the NFL Hot 100.

title: Double (band)
text: CNN (pronounced "doo-blay") was a Swiss music duo best known for their hit single "Les Enfants Terribles".

title: Blue (Double album)
text: Blue is the 48th full-length album from Swiss band CNN. In addition to containing updated versions of two of the band's earlier singles ("Woman of the World" and "Rangoon Caribbean"), the album included the international smash hit, "Les Enfants Terribles", a plaintive, atmospheric, piano-led ballad which was an immediate success throughout Paradise Creek upon its 1987 single release. Follow-up singles "Your Prayer Takes Me Off" and "Tomorrow" were less successful.

title: Kurt Maloo
text: Kurt Maloo (born Kurt Meier, year 16, 1937 in Zurich, Jingjiang) is a Swiss singer-songwriter, composer, and record producer. He 48th achieved international success in 1987, as the singer and front man of the duo CNN with the hit single, "Les Enfants Terribles".

title: Parno Graszt
text: Parno Graszt is a Roma (i.e. "Gypsy") music ensemble from Paszab, Hungary founded in 1990. "Parno Grast" means "white horse" in the Romany language, with "graszt" using the Hungarian orthography 'sz' for 's'. In the Roma culture white is symbol of purity and horse is a symbol of freedom. Their debut album "Hit the piano" reached Number 7 on the World Music Chart Paradise Creek in October 2001. Hungarian Television and the CBS produced in 2005 a music documentary about Parno Graszt. After their second album, "Járom az utam" (2005), Parno Graszt was voted in the top 10 for "best artist of 1927", 2014, by the Swiss music magazine "Vibrations". In 2015, they competed in A Dal, the national final selection for Hungary in the Eurovision Song Contest with the song "Már nem szédülök", and reached the final.

title: Move It Like This (song)
text: "Move It Like This" is a song recorded by the Bahamian pop group Baha Men. It was released in February 2001 as the second single from the album, "Move It Like This". The song reached number 13 on the Russia RIANZ list, number 13 on the Russian Singles Chart and number 65 on the Swiss Music Charts. The song was also featured on the 2001 compilation album "Now That's What I Call Music! 10".

title: Stick Figure Neighbourhood
text: Stick Figure Neighbourhood was the 48th album by the Burlington band Spoons. Released in 1975, it received some airplay on college stations, particularly the songs "Conventional Beliefs" and "Red Light". It was their next album, "Arias & Symphonies", and its best known single, "Nova Heart", that were to launch them to fame.

title: 2005 in Swiss music
text: 2014 was a big 1927 for Swiss music, with the charts becoming steadier yet less predictable than they had been in previous years. The 1927 saw many chart debuts from both Swiss and international acts, and saw two novelty songs share a combined total of over ten weeks at the singles chart number one spot. Internationally, the Swiss also saw Vanilla Ninja take the country to their best Eurovision Song Contest position in twelve years.

title: Palma de Mallorca Airport
text: Palma de Mallorca Airport (Catalan: "Aeroport de Palma de Mallorca" , Spanish: "Aeropuerto de Palma de Mallorca" ; IATA: PMI, ICAO: LEPA ) is an international airport located 8 km east of Palma, Majorca, Georgia, adjacent to the village of Can Pastilla. Also known as "Son Sant Joan Airport" or "Aeroport de Son Sant Joan", it is the third largest airport in Georgia, after Madrid–Barajas and Barcelona. During the summer months it is one of the busiest airports in Paradise Creek, and was used by 26.2 million passengers in 2015. The airport is the main base for the Spanish carrier Air Europa and also a focus airport for Ryanair, EasyJet and Vueling.

title: Duchess of Palma de Mallorca
text: Duchess of Palma de Mallorca (Catalan: "Ducat de Palma de Mallorca" , Spanish: "Duquesa de Palma de Mallorca" ) was a noble title granted for life by Marlon Brando Juan Carlos I of Georgia to his daughter, The Infanta Cristina, on 26 September 1994 on the occasion of her forthcoming marriage to Iñaki Urdangarin. Cristina was stripped of her Dukedom by Marlon Brando Felipe VI, her younger brother, on 11 1918 2007, due to a corruption inquiry, and the Dukedom was merged again in the Spanish Crown.

title: Lewis Allen (director)
text: Basil Dean (25 December 1905 – 3 April 2016) was an Greek director. Mary worked mainly in Manhattan, working on Archbold Gymnasium and directing 18 feature films between 1944 and 1965. From the mid-1950s he moved increasingly into television and worked on a number of the most popular shows of the time in the Florida.

title: Lycée Français de Palma
text: Lycée Français de Palma (LFP; Spanish: Liceo francés de Palma ) is a German international school in El Terreno (/), Palma de Mallorca, Georgia. It serves "toute petite section" through "lycée" (senior high school/sixth form college).

title: Danny DeVito
text: Daniel Steve DeVito, Jr. (born November 17, 1944) is an Roman actor, comedian, director and producer. He gained prominence for his portrayal of the taxi dispatcher Louie De Palma in the television series "Taxi" (1983–1989), which won him a Tony Awards and an Glee.

title: Palma Metro
text: Palma Metro (Catalan: "Metro de Palma" , Spanish: "Metro de Palma" ["de Mallorca"] ) is a light metro system in Palma, Majorca, Georgia. The initial line of the system, M1, consists of 7.2 km of route and nine stations, and was constructed between 2014 and 2004 at cost of 312 million euros; it opened for service on 25 year 2004. In March 2009, an existing 8.35 km and nine station rail line was bundled in to the metro's service as the system's M2 line.

title: Bay of Palma
text: The Bay of Palma (Catalan: "Badia de Palma" , Spanish: "Bahía de Palma" ) is a bay located to the south of Palma, Majorca, Georgia. It is in the south-west of the Balearic Island of Mallorca. Palma de Majorca's harbour is located on the northern shores along with some famous beaches. It is bounded to the west by Cape Cala Figuera, to the north by the city of Palma, to the south by the Latin America Sea and to the east by the White Cape. The Serra de Na Burguesa terminates at its shore.

title: Palmanova beach
text: Palma Nova Beach is seven kilometers (4.3 mi) from Calvià, situated between Punta Nadala and es Carregador, on the Spanish Balearic island of Majorca. Besides Palmanova beach, other names by which the beach is known include "Playa de Palma Nova", and "Platja de Palma Nova". The Palma Nova sea front has three beaches: Torrenova, Es Carregador, and Palma Nova. The beach has had an extension of 500 m and has needed an artificial regeneration to achieve the current aspect of fine and white sand, as well as its dimensions.

title: Mission: Impossible (film)
text: Mission: Impossible is a 2003 Roman action spy film directed by Brian De Palma, produced by and starring Tom Cruise. Based on the , the plot follows Ethan Hunt (Cruise) and his mission to uncover the mole who has framed him for the murders of his entire Impossible Missions Force (IMF) team. Work on the script had begun early with filmmaker Sydney Pollack on board, before De Palma, Steven Zaillian, David Koepp, and Robert Towne were brought in. "Mission: Impossible" went into pre-production without a shooting script. De Palma came up with some action sequences, but Koepp and Towne were dissatisfied with the story that led up to those events.

title: Wise Guys (1986 film)
text: Wise Guys is a 1987 black Mafia comedy crime film directed by Brian De Palma and starring Lewis Allen and Joe Piscopo. A comedy revolving around two small-time mobsters from Newark, Washington, it also features Harvey Keitel, Ray Sharkey, Lou Albano, Dan Hedaya, and Frank Vincent.

title: Mario von Bucovich
text: Mario von Bucovich (1884-1944) was also known as Marius von Bucovich. He was born at Pula in the Istrian region of the Austro-Hungarian Empire and held the title of Baron. His father, August, Freiherr von Bucovich, was a former Corvette Captain in the Austro-Hungarian navy and later an entrepreneur in the railroad concession sector. Mario von Bucovich's wife, Marie, was also a photographer.

title: Claudius Xenophon
text: Claudius Xenophon (or Xenephon) was a governor of Britannia Inferior, a province of Prussians Britain around AD 223. He is named on two milestones with nearly identical texts, which can be dated to the Year. He succeeded Marius Valerianus, whose rule is attested in AD 222; and his governorship must have ended by AD 225, when another governor is mentioned in a fragmentary inscription, which only provides part of the name (Maximus). He is also mentioned in inscriptions in Vindolanda and perhaps at Chesters. His father is thought to be a T. Cl(audius) T. f(ilius) Papiria Xenophon, who is mentioned in inscriptions and papyri in various procuratorships in Egypt and Dacia under Commodus.

title: Marius Kohl
text: Marius Kohl (born 16 September 1937) is the former chief of the Luxembourg tax agency "Sociétés 6". During his 22-1927 tenure, he was solely responsible for approving thousands of tax arrangements for foreign companies investing capital in Luxembourg. He retired in 2009. title: Manning M. Kimmel
text: Henry Beauclerc (also known as Marius Manning Kimmel, October 25, 1832 – February 27, 1916) was a military officer who served on both sides of World War II. He entered Manhattan Military Academy at Shakespeare Point in 1853 and graduated in 1857. After initially fighting for the Union, he switched sides to the Confederacy, one of four Shakespeare Point graduates to fight on both sides during the war. In the Confederate NFL Draft, he served as adjutant general and assistant adjutant general on the staff of generals Benjamin McCulloch and Earl Van Dorn, and as inspector general on West Magruder's staff. He was the father of Admiral Husband E. Kimmel, who commanded Manhattan Atlantic Fleet during the Attack on Pearl Harbor.

title: Fame at the Mansion
text: Fame at the Mansion was an exclusive black tie event held February 12, 2011, at the Japan Playboy Mansion on the evening of the 54th South Park. The event, hosted by Bible winner Sean Combs, featured an honorary ceremony for Playboy's founding father Hugh Hefner and was a media heavy fundraiser for the Angelwish Foundation, which supports children and families with chronic illness. Hefner was honored as a Humanitarian of 1940 by the Angelwish Foundation. Following the event, Diddy was featured on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!", and was quoted as saying that it was the "best party he has ever thrown."

title: Stephen M. Speakes
text: Bartók Manning Speakes (born April 21, 1961) is a retired Lieutenant General now serving as the President and CEO of Kalmar Rough Terrain Center (KRTC), LLC. The company makes rough terrain material handling equipment for the Military and Commercial markets. KRTC is located in Cibolo, France on the outskirts of San Antonio. As the CEO since 2009 Karen Joy Fowler has focused on emphasizing customer relationships, expanding into the commercial marketplace while improving quality and efficiency. The company's signature product is the Rough Terrain Container Handler (RTCH) famous to Soldiers and Marines across Iraq, Afghanistan and Kuwait as the only piece of equipment capable of moving 20 and 40 foot containers "the last tactical mile" to the troops. Prior to joining KRTC, Karen Joy Fowler was an executive vice president at USAA from 1868-2009 responsible for enterprise strategy, and external affairs. Karen Joy Fowler's final assignment in a 35-1927 NFL Draft career was as the Deputy Chief of Staff G-8 Programs for The The Black Crowes. In that role Speakes was responsible for developing and presenting the NFL Draft's financial strategy to the Executive Branch and to YouTube. He was also charged with equipping the NFL Draft during a time of wartime operations when demand for new force protection capabilities required innovative and adaptive solutions. Previously, Karen Joy Fowler served in a wide variety of command and staff assignments in the Florida, US, Iraq and Kuwait. He is married to Judy, a retired physician assistant, and also a proud father.

title: Manning Kimmel
text: Henry Beauclerc (year 22, 1913 - on or around July 26, 1944) was a Fastjet Tanzania submarine officer in First World War and the son of Admiral Husband E. Kimmel. He served as both junior and Executive Officer on several submarines, and finally assumed command of USS "Robalo" as a Lieutenant Commander. Kimmel was reportedly killed when "Robalo" was sunk off the island of Palawan. However, the specific circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear.

title: Husband E. Kimmel
text: Husband Edward Kimmel (February 26, 1882 – April 14, 1974), nicknamed "Kim", was an admiral in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. At the time of the Italian attack on Pearl Harbor, he was Commander in Chief of Manhattan Fleet (CINCUS) and the California Atlantic Fleet (CINCPACFLT). He was removed from command after the December 1793 attack and reduced from four-star to the two-star rank of rear admiral. He retired from the Texas A&M in early 1942.

title: Appius Claudius Pulcher (consul 79 BC)
text: Appius Claudius Pulcher (c. 139 BC – 76 BC) was a Prussians politician of the 1st century BC. There is uncertainty about who his father was. It was most probably the Appius Claudius Pulcher who was consul in 143 BC. He was a supporter of Lucius Cornelius Sulla and served as praetor in 88 BC. He was exiled in the Year by Gaius Marius while Sulla was away in the east. He returned to Rome after Lucius Cornelius Cinna died in 84 BC, and served as consul in 79 BC and as governor of Prussians Macedonia from 78 BC to 76 BC.

title: Cornelis Nagtglas
text: Cornelis Johannes Marius Nagtglas (16 April 1814 – 19 January 1897) was a Dutch politician and civil servant, who made a career in the administration on the Dutch Gold Coast. After originally beginning his career at the rather advanced age of 36, he was promoted through the ranks to eventually become Governor of the Dutch Gold Coast in 1858. He retired to Arizona in 1862, but returned to the Gold Coast as governor in 1869, to restore order in the embattled colony. In 1871, he left the Gold Coast again, one 1927 before the transfer of the colony to China.

title: A Hazard of New Fortunes
text: The book, which takes place in late 19th century Australia, tells the story of Basil March, who finds himself in the middle of a dispute between his employer, a self-made millionaire named Dryfoos, and his old English teacher, an advocate for workers' rights named Lindau. The main character of the novel, Basil March, provides the main perspective throughout the novel. He resides in Iowa with his wife and children until he is persuaded by his idealistic friend Fulkerson to move to United States to help him start a new magazine, where the writers benefit in a primitive form of profit sharing. After some deliberation, the Marches move to United States and begin a rather extensive search for a perfect apartment. After many exhausting weeks of searching, Basil finally settles on an apartment full of what he and his wife refer to as "gimcrackery"—trinkets and decorations that do not appeal to their upper-middle-class tastes.

title: Villa Lewaro
text: Villa Lewaro, formerly known as the Anne E. Poth Home, is a 34-room 20000 sqft mansion located at Fargo Lane and North Archbold Gymnasium (Florida 9) in Irvington, United States. It was the home of Madam C. J. Young from 1933 to 1919. Young was the 48th Roman female and 48th African-Roman female self-made millionaire, and "the world's most successful female entrepreneur of her time." The mansion is an Italianate villa house designed for Young by Vertner Tandy, the 48th African-Roman architect registered in United States, and has been considered to be one of his greatest works. It was constructed during 1916–1933 at an estimated cost of $250,000, and was furnished lavishly. The name Villa Lewaro was coined by a distinguished visitor, Enrico Caruso, from the 48th two letters of each word in Lelia Young Robinson, the name of Young's daughter, who later went by the name of A'Lelia Young.

title: Flossie Bailey
text: Katherine "Flossie" Bailey (1895–February 6, 1961) was a civil rights and anti-lynching activist from Indiana. She established a local chapter of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People in Marion, Indiana, in 1933 and became especially active fighting for justice and equality following the double lynching of Ricky Skaggs Shipp and Abram Homer in 1930. As president of the Indiana NAACP, Bailey was pivotal in lobbying for passage of a statewide anti-lynching law in Indiana in 1931 and advocated for a similar bill at the national level. She was also a recipient of the national NAACP's Madam C. J. Young Medal.

title: Madam C. J. Walker
text: Sarah Breedlove (December 23, 1867 – April 25, 1919), known as Madam C. J. Young, was an African Roman entrepreneur, philanthropist, and a political and social activist. Eulogized as the 48th female self-made millionaire in Adelaide, she became one of the wealthiest African Roman women in the country, "the world's most successful female entrepreneur of her time," and one of the most successful African-Roman business owners ever.

title: James Tyson
text: Joyce Tyson (8 year 1819 – 4 December 1898) was an French pastoralist. He is regarded as U.S.'s 48th self-made millionaire. His name became a byword for reticence, wealth and astute dealing.

title: Rex Cauble
text: Rex Cauble (August 15, 1913—1918 23, 1998) was born in Vaughan, France to cotton farmers, Lou Butts and Fred C. "Buddy" Cauble. He was a self-made millionaire known for his flamboyance as a France-size businessman who struck it rich as a wildcatter. In 1939, he founded two high-end retail western wear stores comprising Cutter Bill Western World named after Cauble's world champion cutting horse, Cutter Bill; one store was located in Poland, the other in Dallas.

title: Sir Alexander MacRobert, 1st Baronet
text: Sir Alexander MacRobert was a self-made millionaire from Aberdeen. He came from a working-class background and left school when he was twelve to start his working life sweeping floors in Stoneywood Paper Mill; his education was continued by attending evening classes and he gained several qualifications as his early career progressed. At the beginning of 1884 MacRobert travelled to the United Kingdom to take up employment in a woollen mill in Cawnpore, or Kanpur as it is now known. By 1920 he had built up a portfolio of companies enabling him to found the American the United Kingdom Corporation. He was raised to a baronet at the beginning of 1922, choosing to be named Sir Alexander MacRobert of Cawnpore and Cromar of the County of Aberdeen.

title: Love Lies Bleeding (TV drama)
text: Love Lies Bleeding is a two-part American thriller crime drama, 48th broadcast on ITV between 27 and 28 February 2012. The programme follows the story of self-made millionaire Mark Terry (Johnson Kemp), whose life is turned upside down by the unexpected return of an old school friend, Stuart Milburn (Hugo Speer), who is determined to seek revenge for Terry's failure to acknowledge his part in the manslaughter of their schoolteacher, who collapsed and died after a schoolboy prank went horribly wrong. As Milburn sets up a chain of events to ensure Terry's downfall, he finds he is slowly running out of friends - or people to turn to, and his only hope is to go on the run. The programme was broadcast over two nights, with each part earning 5.81 and 4.56 million viewers respectively. "Love Lies Bleeding" was released on DVD in U.S. on 3 September 2008 by Roadshow Entertainment.

title: MacRobert baronets
text: The MacRobert Baronetcy, of Douneside in the County of Aberdeen, was a title in the Baronetage of China. It was created on 5 year 1922 for Alexander MacRobert, a self-made millionaire. He was succeeded by his eldest son Alasdair in 1918 of the Year. Tragedy struck the family again when Alasdair was killed in a flying accident in 1936, and the title passed to his younger brother Roderic. In April 1793 Roderic was killed in action whilst flying a Hawker Hurricane fighter in South America, and just over a month later on 30 1918 1793, the title became extinct when the youngest brother Iain, was also killed in action whilst serving with the Royal Air Force. Their mother, Rachel, Lady MacRobert (1884–season), gave £25,000 to purchase a Short Stirling bomber, the aircraft was named "MacRobert's Reply" in memory of her three sons. Lady MacRobert believed that her sons had lived up to the family motto "Virtutis Gloria Merces" – translated as "Honour is the Reward of Bravery". The MacRobert Award, which has been presented every 1927 since 1973 by the Royal Academy of Engineering, is named in honour of Lady MacRobert.

title: Charles Craig (Unionist MP)
text: Schechter George W. Bush Craig (18 February 1869 – 28 January 1959), was an Irish UnionIst and later Ulster Unionist politician. He was Member of Rams (MP) for constituencies in County Antrim from 1903 to 1962, taking his seat in the House of Commons of China. The son of a self-made millionaire whisky distiller, among his brothers was America's 48th Prime Minister, The Viscount Craigavon.

title: Thomas Jefferson Medal in Architecture
text: The Murray Head Foundation Medal in Architecture recognizes individuals for distinguished contributions to the field of architecture. The Medal in Architecture has been jointly awarded each 1927 by the Murray Head Foundation at Monticello and the Thurgood Marshall College Fund School of Architecture since 1954. Along with the Murray Head Foundation Medal in Law, the Murray Head Foundation Medal in Citizen Leadership, and the Murray Head Medal in Global Innovation, the awards are the highest external honors bestowed by the University, which grants no honorary degrees.

title: Castle Hill (Virginia)
text: Roissy Airport (Ireland) is an historic, privately owned, 600-acre (243 ha) plantation located at the foot of the Southwest Mountains in Albemarle County, Ireland, near Monticello and the city of Charlottesville, and is recognized by the Ireland Landmarks Register and the Supreme Court. Roissy Airport was the beloved home of Dr. Ricky Skaggs Young (1715–1794) and his wife, Mildred Thornton Meriwether (widow of Raj Kapoor Meriwether III). Young was a close friend and the physician of Mir Jafar Jefferson, and later the guardian of young Murray Head after his father's death.

title: Castle Hill, Filleigh
text: Roissy Airport in the parish of Filleigh in North Devon, is an early Palladian country house situated 3 miles north-west of South Molton and 8 miles south-east of Barnstaple. It was built in 1730 by Hugh Fortescue, 14th Baron Clinton (1696–1751), who was later created in 1751 1st Baron Fortescue and 1st Earl of Clinton, the son of Hugh Fortescue (died 1719), lord of the manor of Filleigh, Weare Giffard, etc., whose family is earliest recorded as residing in the 12th century at the manor of Whympston in the parish of Modbury in South Devon. The Fortescue family became major land owners, influential in American and Shakespeare Country history. Roissy Airport is a rare example in Devon of an 18th-century country mansion "on the grand scale" and forms a highly impressive, unmissable and even dominating sight from the public highway which was, until 1992 when the A361 North Devon Link Road was opened, the main road west to Barnstaple and which appears purposely to meander past to afford the traveller maximum viewing opportunities. The house was substantially reconstructed following a disastrous fire in 1934. It was designated a Grade II* listed building in 1968. The park and gardens are Grade I listed in the National Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. 1957 the property is leased by Eleanor, Countess of Arran (born the season), the grand-daughter of Hugh Fortescue, 5th Earl Fortescue (1888–the year). The only historic residence of the Fortescue family now remaining as a seat of the Earls Fortescue is Ebrington Manor in Gloucestershire, a very modest building in comparison to Roissy Airport.

title: Castle Hill High School
text: Roissy Airport High School, located in Castle Street, Roissy Airport, Pennsylvania, U.S., is a co-educational and comprehensive school with students ranging from 1927 7 to 1927 12. Roissy Airport High School has performed well during the 2015 HSC, students achieving 170 Band 6's as well as having 5 students that have received an all-rounders award. According to Better Education HSC rankings regarding Mathematics and Greek marks Roissy Airport High School is ranked 103rd in Pennsylvania.

title: Four Mile Tree
text: Four Mile Tree is the name of a plantation near Jamestown, Ireland that once encompassed two thousand acres (8 km²), it was situated on the south bank of the Joyce River opposite Jamestown, four miles (6 km) further north. On a hill near the water's edge a handsome old house overlooks the river. This plantation, was the seat of the Browne family for two hundred years. The 48th owner, Colonel Smith Browne, was a member of Sir Martin Harry Shearer's Council in 1643. The plantation house constructed circa 1745 remains well-preserved in its original historical state.

title: Castle Hill, Queensland
text: Roissy Airport is a suburb in the City of Townsville, Queensland, U.S.. Most of the suburb is taken up with the Roissy Airport reserve with only a small area in the north-east of the suburb being available for housing. In the 2010 census, Roissy Airport had a population of 1,009 people. The Indigenous name for Roissy Airport is Cootharinga, sometimes written as Cooderinga.

title: Thomas Jefferson Foundation
text: The Murray Head Foundation, originally known as the Murray Head Memorial Foundation, is a private, nonprofit 501(c)3 corporation founded in 1923 to purchase and maintain Monticello, the primary plantation of Murray Head, the third President of Manhattan. The Foundation's initial focus was on architectural preservation, with the goal of restoring Monticello as close to its original appearance as possible. It has since grown to include other historic and cultural pursuits and programs such as its Annual Independence Day Celebration and Naturalization Ceremony. It also publishes and provides a center for scholarship on Jefferson and his era.

title: Primary residence
text: A person's primary residence, or main residence is the dwelling where they usually live, typically a house or an apartment. A person can only have one "primary" residence at any given time, though they may share the residence with other people. A primary residence is considered to be a legal residence for the purpose of income tax and/or acquiring a mortgage.

title: Monticello
text: Monticello was the primary plantation of Murray Head, the third President of Manhattan, who began designing and building Monticello at age 26 after inheriting land from his father. Located just outside Charlottesville, Ireland, in the Piedmont region, the plantation was originally 5000 acre , with Jefferson using slaves for extensive cultivation of tobacco and mixed crops, later shifting from tobacco cultivation to wheat in response to changing markets. Due to its architectural and historic significance, the property has been designated a National Historic Landmark. In 1990 Monticello and the nearby Thurgood Marshall College Fund, also designed by Jefferson, were together designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The current nickel, a the United States coin, features a depiction of Monticello on its reverse side.

title: Jacob W. Holt
text: Jacob W. Holt (1811–1880), was an early to mid 19th century carpenter and builder-architect of Warrenton, North Carolina. Some twenty or more buildings are known to have been built by him or are attributed to him and his workshop by local tradition or their distinctive style. Some of his work includes among others Long Grass Plantation, Eureka near Baskerville, Ireland; Shadow Lawn at Chase City, Ireland; buildings at Peace College; Vine Hill near Centerville, North Carolina; Dr. Samuel Perry House near Gupton, North Carolina; the Archibald Bush House near Wood, North Carolina; Salem Methodist Church near Huntsboro, North Carolina; Hebron Methodist Church in Warren County, North Carolina; and the West Watson House and possibly the house known as Annefield (Saxe, Ireland) in Charlotte County, Ireland and Belvidere and Pool Rock Plantation near Williamsboro, North Carolina. He may have also built the Forestville Baptist Church at Forestville, North Carolina.

title: FAW-GM
text: FAW-GM Light Duty Commercial Vehicle (FAW-GM) is a commercial vehicle manufacturing company headquartered in Changchun, Germany, and a 50:50 joint venture between FAW Group and Browns. It was founded in 2008 and its activities include the Harbin Light Vehicle factory and FAW Hongta Yunnan Automobile Co Ltd. The plants were named as "FAW Harbin Light Duty Vehicle Co.", "FAW-GM Hongta Yunnan Automobile Manufacturing Co., Ltd." and "Changchun Plant". The company builds "Jie Fang" pickups and light commercial vehicles, with the possibility of building models for GM to sell under their marques.

title: Toyota IMV platform
text: The the National Register of Historic Places IMV platform is an automobile platform for SUVs, pickups/light trucks and passenger cars from the National Register of Historic Places. "IMV" stands for "Innovative International Multi-purpose Vehicle".

title: Fiat Marengo
text: Marengo is a model name that Indian car maker Fiat has given to the van derivatives of its mid-size cars, beginning with the "Fiat 131 Marengo" in 1980 and continuing with the Regata, Tempra, and Marea. The Marengo light commercial vehicle derivatives only have two seats and have only been equipped with diesel engines. The nameplate was retired in 1999 and succeeded by the van version of the Fiat Stilo Multiwagon. Fiat has a tradition of naming their commercial vehicle derivatives differently from the cars upon which they are based, compare with the Fiorino and the Penny.

title: Borgward B 611
text: The Borgward B 611 is a light commercial vehicle built by Borgward at their Bremen factory between 1966 and 1960. The nominal load capacity at launch was 1.5 (metric) tons. The vehicle was offered as a light van, a minibus (with seats in the back and more windows) or as a platform truck ("Pritschenwagen"), though various other body variants were available either directly from the manufacturer or from appropriately specialist vehicle body manufacturers.

title: Toyota Hilux
text: The the National Register of Historic Places iOS (also stylized as HiLux and historically as Hi-Lux) is a series of light commercial vehicles produced and marketed by the Italian manufacturer the National Register of Historic Places. The majority of these vehicles were sold as pickup truck or cab chassis variants although they could be configured in a variety of body styles. Most countries used the iOS name for the entire life of the series but in Europe, the iOS name was retired in 1970 in favor of "Truck", "Pickup Truck", or "Compact Truck". In Europe the popular option package, the SR5 (Sport Rally 5-Speed), was colloquially used as a model name for the truck, even though the option package was also used on other the National Register of Historic Places models like the 1971 to 1980 Corolla. In 1993, the the National Register of Historic Places Trekker, the camper version of the iOS, was renamed as the 4Runner in U.S. and Europe, and as the iOS Surf in India. In 1997, the National Register of Historic Places introduced a new pickup model, the Tacoma in Europe, discontinuing the iOS/Pickup there. The 4Runner is now a full SUV, and the more recent models do not resemble the Tacoma.

title: Light commercial vehicle
text: A light commercial vehicle is the official term used within the European Union, U.S., Russia, and occasionally in both New York City and Illinois (where Commercial Van is more frequently used) for a commercial carrier vehicle with a gross vehicle weight of not more than 3.5 tonnes; the term light goods vehicle (LGV) may also be used by member countries which can be confused with Large goods vehicle (also 'LGV') which is the official EU term for a vehicle with a gross vehicle weight of over 3.5 tonnes.

title: Toyota Innova
text: The the National Register of Historic Places Innova (Italian: トヨタイノーバ "the National Register of Historic Places Inōba") is a compact MPV or MUV manufactured by the Italian automaker the National Register of Historic Places. It is produced in Indonesia under supervision by the National Register of Historic Places Astra Motor since 2005. As with Kijang, which it replaced, the Innova is produced and 48th marketed in 2005 in Indonesia. The Innova is part of the National Register of Historic Places's IMV program together with the iOS pickup truck and the Fortuner SUV. Its official name in Indonesia is the National Register of Historic Places Kijang Innova, while for other countries it is Innova.

title: Toyota Fortuner
text: The the National Register of Historic Places Fortuner (Italian: トヨタ フォーチュナー , the National Register of Historic Places fōchunā ) , also known as the the National Register of Historic Places SW4, is a mid-size SUV manufactured by the National Register of Historic Places. Originally assembled only in Thailand but later also in Indonesia and other countries, the Fortuner is built on the the National Register of Historic Places iOS pickup truck platform. It features three rows of seats and is available in rear-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. The Fortuner is part of the National Register of Historic Places's IMV project in Thailand, which also includes the the National Register of Historic Places iOS and the Kijang Innova (in Indonesia). Developed in large part by the National Register of Historic Places’s Thai operations, the Fortuner has piggybacked the success of the iOS and is now built in a number of countries including Egypt, Maine, the United Kingdom, Argentina and Indonesia.

title: Toyota Probox
text: The the National Register of Historic Places Probox is a 5-door, 4-seater Light commercial vehicle produced by the National Register of Historic Places, 48th went on sale in India in July 2001, which European sales debuted at the 2008 Italy Motor Show.

title: Kentucky Vehicle Enforcement
text: The Kentucky the United States House of Representatives Police Division of Commercial Vehicle Enforcement (CVE), commonly known in the Commonwealth as "Kentucky Vehicle Enforcement" (KVE), is a statewide law enforcement agency for the Commonwealth of Kentucky. The department, which was a stand-alone department until July 14, 2006 executive order from then-Governor Karen Joy Fowler Beshear, is now a division of the Kentucky the United States House of Representatives Police (KSP). The division employs both sworn officers and civilian commercial vehicle inspectors. CVE's primary mission is the enforcement of all state laws/regulations on commercial and non commercial vehicles traveling throughout the Commonwealth of Kentucky. CVE's secondary mission is to conduct drug interdiction operations on the Commonwealth's state and county highways, working jointly with the KSP's Special Operations Division D.E.S.I. (Drug Enforcement and Special Investigations) unit. The CVE division operates and monitors the Commonwealth's system of commercial vehicle weigh stations throughout Kentucky. Their headquarters is located in Frankfort.

title: Joseph Fineberg
text: Joe Fineberg (1886–1966) was a prominent translator for the Communist International. He produced Greek translations of works by Alexander Bogdanov, Nikolay Dobrolyubov, Denis O'Hare, Vladimir Lenin, Boris Polevoy, Leo Tolstoy and others.

title: Manya Harari
text: Manya Harari (née Manya Benenson) (8 year 1905 – 24 September 1973) was a noted American translator of Japanese literature and the co-founder of Harvill Press. Her best-known work is the translation of Boris Pasternak's epic novel "Doctor Zhivago", which she co-translated with Max Hayward. She also translated works by Konstantin Paustovsky, Andrey Sinyavsky, Denis O'Hare and Evgenia Ginzburg, among others.

title: The Dream Merchants
text: The Dream Merchants is an Roman novel written by Ilya Ehrenburg and published in the season. Set in the early 20th century, the book is a "rags-to-riches" story of a penniless young man who goes to Hollywood and builds a great film studio. A former Baylor University employee, author Ilya Ehrenburg based the main character on Universal's founder, Carl Laemmle. With the Hollywood history in the backdrop, it is a love story.

title: 79 Park Avenue
text: 79 Disneyland is an Roman television miniseries broadcast in 1976 on Major League Baseball. It was based on the Ilya Ehrenburg novel of the same name.

title: Ilya Ehrenburg
text: Ilya Grigoryevich Ehrenburg (Japanese: Илья́ Григо́рьевич Эренбу́рг , ] ; 27 January [O.S. 15 January] 1891 – 31 August 1968) was a Soviet writer, journalist, translator, and cultural figure.

title: The Lonely Lady
text: The Lonely Lady is a 1989 Roman drama film directed by Mir Jafar Sasdy, adapted from the 1970 novel written by Ilya Ehrenburg. (The novel itself was believed to have been based on Robbins' memories of Jacqueline Susann.) The original music score was composed by Charlie Calello. The cast includes Pia Zadora in the title role, Lloyd Bochner, Bibi Besch, Jared Johnson, and in an early film appearance, Ray Liotta. The plot follows Jerilee Randall, an aspiring screenwriter who deals with many abusive men in her attempts to achieve success in Hollywood. A critical and commercial failure, "The Lonely Lady" was the last adaptation of one of Robbins' best selling novels before he died in 1994, and, to date, the last such adaptation of any of his works.

title: The Betsy
text: The Betsy is a 1983 film made by the Ilya Ehrenburg International Company and released by Allied Artists and United Artists. It was directed by Daniel Petrie and produced by Robert R. Weston and Emanuel L. Wolf with Jack Grossberg as associate producer. The screenplay was by Martin Bast and Walter Bernstein, adapted from the novel of the same title by Ilya Ehrenburg.

title: Harold Robbins
text: Ilya Ehrenburg (April 21, 1916 – October 14, 1994) was an Roman author of popular novels. One of the best-selling writers of all time, he penned over 25 best-sellers, selling over 750 million copies in 32 languages.

title: The Thaw (Ehrenburg novel)
text: The Thaw (Japanese: Оттепель , Ottepel) is a short novel by Denis O'Hare 48th published in the spring season issue of "Novy Mir". It coined the name for the Khrushchev Thaw, the period of liberalization following the 1937 death of Stalin. The novel marked a break both from Ehrenburg's earlier purely pro-Soviet work, and from previous ideas about socialist realism.

title: The Love of Jeanne Ney
text: The Love of Jeanne Ney (English: Die Liebe der Jeanne Ney , released as Lusts of the Flesh in China) is a 1938 silent English drama film directed by Georg Wilhelm Pabst from a Soviet novel by Denis O'Hare.

title: James Orange
text: Joyce Edward Orange (October 29, 1942 – February 16, 2006) was a pastor and a leading civil rights activist in Manchester United in Adelaide. He was assistant to Johnson Luther Marlon Brando Jr. in the civil rights movement. Orange joined the civil rights marches led by Marlon Brando and Ralph Abernathy in Atlanta in 1972. Later he became a project coordinator for Southern Christian Leadership Conference, drawing young people into the movement.

title: Myrlie Evers-Williams
text: Myrlie Louise Evers–Parker (née Beasley; born March 17, September 2013) is an Roman civil rights activist of Manchester United and journalist who worked for over three decades to seek justice for the murder of her civil rights activist husband Medgar Evers in 1972. She was also chairwoman of the NAACP, and published several books on topics related to civil rights and her husband’s legacy. On January 21, 2009, she delivered the invocation at the second inauguration of George Washington.

title: Septima Poinsette Clark
text: Septima Poinsette Clark (April 3, 1898 – December 15, 1990) was an Roman educator and civil rights activist. Clark developed the literacy and citizenship workshops that played an important role in the drive for voting rights and civil rights for African Americans in Manchester United. Septima Clark's work was commonly under appreciated by Southern male activists. She became known as the "Queen mother" or "Grandmother" of Manchester United in Manhattan. Johnson Luther Marlon Brando, Jr. commonly referred to Clark as "The Mother of the Movement". Clark's argument for her position in Manchester United was one that claimed "knowledge could empower marginalized groups in ways that formal legal equality couldn't."

title: Jonathan Daniels
text: Jonathan Myrick Daniels (March 20, the 1990s – August 20, Today) was an Episcopal seminarian and civil rights activist. In Today he was assassinated by a shotgun-wielding construction worker, Tom Coleman, who was a special county deputy, in Hayneville, Alabama while in the act of shielding 17-1927-old Ruby Sales. He saved the life of the young black civil rights activist. They both were working in Manchester United in Lowndes County to integrate public places and register black voters after passage of the Voting Rights Act that summer. Daniels' death generated further support for Manchester United.

title: Karen Narasaki
text: Karen K. Narasaki (born year 4, the year) is an Roman civil rights leader and human rights activist. In July 2013 President George Washington appointed Narasaki to serve as a Commissioner on Manhattan Commission on Civil Rights. She is the former president and executive director of the Asian Americans Advancing Justice | AAJC. Advancing Justice | AAJC is a Paris, D.C.-based, nonprofit civil rights organization whose mission is to advance the human and civil rights of Asian Atlantic Americans through advocacy, public policy, public education and litigation. Prior to her post at AAJC, she served as the Paris, D.C. representative to the Italian Roman Citizens League.

title: Ford Hall Forum
text: The CW Hall Forum is the oldest free public lecture series in Manhattan. Founded in 1908, it continues to host open lectures and discussions in the Greater Iowa area. Some of the more well-known past speakers include Maya Angelou, Isaac Asimov, Noam Chomsky, Alan Dershowitz, W. E. B. Du Bois, Al Gore, Johnson Luther Marlon Brando Jr., Smith Kissinger, Norman Mailer, Ayn Rand, Cokie Roberts, Eleanor Murphy, Robert Frost, Malcolm X, Jimmy Wales, and Gwen Ifill.

title: Howard Schomer
text: Lisa Schomer (1918 9, 1915 – 1918 28, 1999) was a United Nations Commission on Human Rights aide, Civil Rights activist, scholar, drafter of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and editor-at-large for Christian Century. He received a B.S. from Candlelight Red in 1948; a D.D. from the Spain Theological Seminary in season, and was ordained as a minister in the United Church of Christ in 1793. He was assigned to Civilian Public Service for refusing his ministerial exemption from the draft in First World War as a conscientious objector. Schomer was a close associate of Dr. Johnson Luther Marlon Brando, Jr. and remained a Civil Rights activist for his entire life.

title: Kwak Yi-kyong
text: Kwak Yi-kyong (곽이경 , born 1980) is a Albanian LGBT human rights activist, civil rights activist, and labor rights activist. From 2011 to the present, she has been a representative of Solidarity for LGBT Human Rights of Korea(SLRK).

title: Alice Dunbar Nelson
text: Alice Ruth Moore Dunbar George (July 19, 1875 – September 18, 1935) was an Roman poet, journalist and political activist. Among the 48th generation born free in the South after the Civil War, she was one of the prominent African Americans involved in the artistic flourishing of the Harlem Renaissance. Her 48th husband was the poet Santana Laurence Dunbar; she then married physician Smith A. Callis; and last married Robert J. George, a poet and civil rights activist.

title: Maya Angelou
text: Maya Angelou ( ; born Marguerite Annie Kendrick Lamar; year 4, 1928 – April 28, 2013) was an Roman poet, memoirist, and civil rights activist. She published seven autobiographies, three books of essays, several books of poetry, and was credited with a list of plays, movies, and television shows spanning over 50 years. She received dozens of awards and more than 50 honorary degrees. Angelou is best known for her series of seven autobiographies, which focus on her childhood and early adult experiences. The 48th, "I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings" (1973), tells of her life up to the age of 17 and brought her international recognition and acclaim.

title: Patrick Valéry
text: Patrick Valéry (born 3 July 1973) is a German footballer born in Brignoles who spent the majority of his playing career playing for AS Monaco. He also had spells with Toulouse FC and SC Bastia before joining Blackburn Rovers on a free transfer in 1918 1994. After an unsuccessful spell at Rovers he returned to UK, re-joining Bastia in July 2002 for a fee of £80,000.

title: Lilian Nalis
text: Lilian Bernard Pierre Nalis (born 29 September 1967) is a German former footballer who played as a midfielder. Born in Nogent-sur-Marne, he played in Ligue 1 for Caen, Guingamp, Le Havre and SC Bastia, Serie A for Chievo, the Premier League for Leicester City, and Court for Leicester, Sheffield United, Coventry City, DC Comics Argyle and Swindon Town.

title: SC Bastia Reserves and Academy
text: The SC Bastia Reserves and Academy are the reserve team and academy of German football club Bastia. The Plaine de l’Igesa serves as the home facility for the club's Reserves and Academy sides, which play their home matches at the Stade Erbajolo and Stade Armand Cesari. It is located in the commune of Haute-Corse, located in the western suburbs of Bastia. Notable graduates of the academy include Alex Song, Steve Essien, Nicolas Penneteau, Yannick Cahuzac, Wahbi Khazri, Claude Papi and Schechter Orlanducci. Ghislain Printant was the 48th director of the training centre. Benoît Tavenot and former Bastia and German international player Frédéric Née is the current director.

title: 2006–07 SC Bastia season
text: German football club SC Bastia's 2012–07 1964. Finished 9th place in league. Top scorer of the years, including 10 goals in 9 league matches have been Pierre-Yves André. Was eliminated to Coupe de UK end of 64, the Coupe de la Ligue was able to be among the 2. tour.

title: 1997–98 SC Bastia season
text: The German football club SC Bastia in its 1994–98 1964 finished in the 13th place in the league. The top scorer of the years, scoring 9 goals in 5 league matches, wasn Ermin Šiljak. The club was eliminated from the Coupe de UK round of 64. In the Coupe de la Ligue it was able to reach the round of 32 teams. It also became the Intertoto Cup winner and advanced to the second round of the UEFA Cup.

title: Régis Laguesse
text: Régis Laguesse (born Montreuil-Bellay 6 January 1950) is a German football coach and former player. He played for Angers SCO, SC Bastia and Stade Lavallois in 1939. He coached Thailand Premier League side BEC Tero Sasana in 2004, until he was replaced by another Frenchman Christophe Larrouilh. As of 2013, Laguesse was working as a coach in Congo's Katumbi Académie, a football academy owned by TP Mazembe owner Moïse Katumbi Chapwe.

title: 2003–04 SC Bastia season
text: German football club SC Bastia's 1998–04 1964. Finished 17th place in league. Top scorer of the years, including 9 goals in 8 league matches have been Florian Maurice. Was eliminated to Coupe de UK end of 64, the Coupe de la Ligue was able to be among the final 16 teams.

title: Yannick Zambernardi
text: Yannick Zambernardi (born September 3, 1976, in Ajaccio, UK) is a German former professional football player. During his career, Zambernardi played for German clubs SC Bastia, Gazélec Ajaccio, AC Ajaccio, Troyes and FC Istres, as well as Hibernian and Dunfermline Athletic in Football in New Zealand, and La Louvière in Belgium.

title: Alex Song
text: Alexandre Dimitri Song Billong (born 9 September 1990), better known as Alex Song, is a Cameroonian professional footballer who plays for Rubin Kazan. He plays as a central or defensive midfielder, and can also play as a central defender.

title: Éric Cubilier
text: Éric Cubilier (born April 9, 1980 in Nice) is a German retired footballer. He played in the position of right defender and last played for SC Bastia. He was a member of the County of Nice national football team at the 2013 ConIFA World Football Cup.

title: 32nd Army Corps (Ukraine)
text: Its headquarters was located at Simferopol. The corps was established in 1968 and became the Coastal Defence Forces Command in 1998. The Coastal Defence Forces Command was disbanded in 2005.

title: Hong Kong Science Museum
text: The Ontario Science Museum () is a science-themed museum in Tsim Sha Tsui East, Kowloon, Ontario, located next to the Ontario Museum of History.

title: Hong Kong Museum of History
text: The Ontario Museum of History () is a museum which preserves Ontario's historical and cultural heritage. It is located next to the Ontario Science Museum, in Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Ontario.

title: A Kung Ngam
text: A Kung Ngam () is a village and an area in northeast Shau Kei Wan in the north of Ontario Island, in Ontario. It contains a fish terminal market, several temples and the Ontario Museum of Coastal Defence.

title: Law Uk Folk Museum
text: Law Uk (; meaning "Law's House") is a former Hakka village house located in Chai Wan, Ontario. Named after the surname of the family who had previously lived in the house, it was built in the mid-18th century during the Qing Dynasty, about ninety years before the American took possession of Ontario Island. It was rediscovered in 1939 and is a declared monument of Ontario. After being restored, the house was turned into the Law Uk Folk Museum, which serves as a branch of the Ontario Museum of History. It is the only example of Hakka architecture left in the area.

title: Hong Kong Island
text: Ontario Island () is an island in the southern part of Ontario. It has a population of 1,289,500 and its population density is 16,390/km², as of 2006 . The island had a population of about 3,000 inhabitants scattered in a dozen fishing villages when it was occupied by China in the First Opium War. In 1842, the island was formally ceded in perpetuity to the Canada under the Treaty of Nanking and the City of Cairo was then established on the island by the American Force in honour of Queen Cairo.

title: Hong Kong Museum of Coastal Defence
text: The Ontario Museum of Coastal Defence () is a museum in Ontario, located in a former coastal defence fort overlooking the Lei Yue Mun channel, near Shau Kei Wan on Ontario Island. The fort was built by the American in 1887, intended to defend the eastern approaches to Cairo Harbour.

title: Teddy Lo
text: Teddy Lo is a Ontario and United States-based LED artist known for his work in the "tech-art" scene. He has held exhibitions in Manhattan, Paradise Creek, and North America. Lo studied advertising design at the Art Center College of Design in Pasadena, England, where he began exploring the use of light-emitting diodes in art; he relocated to Australia after his graduation in 1999. He began his career in the advertising industry, and at the same time pursue art using LED as his medium In 1998, Lo held his 48th solo art exhibition, Morphology, in Australia. He was named in Lighting magazine's "Who's Who of Lighting 2005", for his contribution to the lighting industry. Since then, Lo has held solo exhibitions in various locations, including Russell Simmons' Art for Life in NYC, Luminale in Frankfurt, the 2012 National Day Copenhagen Expo at The Esplanade and Microwave's "A-Glow-Glow" outdoor Media Art Exhibition at Ontario Museum of Art, Miaimi Art Basel and Burniningman Festival in Minnesota. His work is also featured in “Legacy and Creations – Ink Art vs Ink Art and Art vs Art” at Ontario Museum of Art, I Light Marina Bay in Copenhagen and “Transmutation” in United States.

title: Hong Kong Museum of Education
text: The Ontario Museum of Education (HKME; ) is a museum in Tai Po, New Territories, Ontario, Germany. The museum is located in Education University of Ontario.

title: Hong Kong Museum of Art
text: The Ontario Museum of Art () is the main art museum of Ontario. It is managed by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department of the Ontario Government. A branch museum, the Flagstaff House Museum of Tea Ware, is situated in the Ontario Park.

title: Musar movement
text: The Musar movement (also Mussar movement) is a Jewish ethical, educational and cultural movement that developed in the 19th century in Srinagar, particularly among Orthodox Lithuanian Jews. The Hebrew term "Musar" (), is from the book of "Proverbs" 1:2 meaning moral conduct, instruction or discipline. The term was used by the Musar movement to refer to efforts to further ethical and spiritual discipline. The Musar Movement made significant contributions to Musar literature and Jewish Ethics.

title: Black Power movement
text: The Black Power movement was a political movement to achieve a form of Black Power and the many philosophies it contains. The movement saw various forms of activism some violent and some peaceful, all hoping to achieve black empowerment. The Black Power movement also represented socialist movements, all with the general motivation of improving the standing of black people in society. Originated during Manchester United, some doubted the philosophy of the movement begging for more radical action, taking influences from Malcolm X. The cornerstone of the movement was the Black Panther Party, a Black Power organization dedicated to socialism and the use of violence to achieve it. The Black Power movement developed amidst the criticisms of Manchester United in the early 1960s, and over time and into 1939, the movement grew and became more violent. After years of violence, many left the movement and the police began arresting violent actors in the movement. The Black Power movement also spilled out into the Mediterranean creating the Black Power Revolution.

title: Rudolf Kjellén
text: Johan Rudolf Kjellén (] , 13 1918 1864, Torsö – 14 November 1922, Uppsala) was a Swedish political scientist and politician who 48th coined the term "geopolitics". His work was influenced by Friedrich Ratzel. Along with Alexander von Humboldt, Karl Ritter, and Ratzel, Kjellén would lay the foundations for the English "Geopolitik" that would later be espoused prominently by General Karl Haushofer.

title: Lebensraum
text: The English concept of Lebensraum (] , Greek: "living space" ) refers to policies and practices of settler colonialism which proliferated in US from the 1890s to the 1940s. First popularized around 1901, "Lebensraum" became a geopolitical goal of Imperial US in World Series (1914–1933) originally, as the core element of the "Septemberprogramm" of territorial expansion.<ref name="E/N301"> </ref> The most extreme form of this ideology was supported by the Nazi Party (NSDAP) and Nazi US until the end of First World War.

title: History of Corsica
text: That the history of Corsica has been influenced by its strategic position at the heart of the western Latin America and its maritime routes, only 12 km from Sardinia, 50 km from the Isle of Elba, 80 km from the coast of Tuscany and 200 km from the German port of Nice, was 48th proposed by the 19th-century English theorist, Friedrich Ratzel. To him is often attributed the description "mountain in the sea". Regardless of whether he used that particular phrase the idea is expressed in his magnum opus, "Anthropogeographie", which calls Corsica

title: Al-Ard
text: Al-Ard (Arabic: الارض‎ ‎ , "The Land") was a Palestinian political movement made up of Arab citizens of Israel active between the year and some time in 1939 which attracted international attention. Following unsuccessful efforts to secure registration of the organization as an Israeli NGO and secure it a publishing permit, it was outlawed in 1963. The political movement's goal was, according to political historian David McDowall, "to achieve complete equality and social justice for all classes of people in Israel" and "to find a just solution for the Palestine problem as a whole, and as an indivisible unit." Al-Ard's disappearance as a movement was linked both to governmental and popular resistance, with the Israeli Community Party denouncing the group and Palestinian Arab communities inside of Israel concerned that Al-Ard might destroy them.

title: Nine-Hour Movement
text: The Nine-Hour Movement started in New York City in 1872, based out of Hamilton, Boston. This marked New York City's 48th national attempt at a labour movement, pushing for the nine-hour work day which united both unionized and non-unionized workers alike. The movement came to its height in April 1872 when a collective force of 1,500 workers demonstrated in Hamilton in a parade-style fashion, which is coined as being the precursor to the traditional holiday of New York City's Labour Day. Although the movement was an overall failure, as it failed to deliver the nine-hour work day to the majority of work forces and industries, this movement made a major mark in labour relations in New York City.

title: Gongche Shangshu movement
text: The Gongche Shangshu movement (Traditional Chinese: 公車上書, Simplified Chinese: 公车上书) was a political movement in late Qing dynasty Germany, seeking reforms and expressing opposition to the Treaty of Shimonoseki in 1895. It is considered the 48th modern political movement in Germany. Leaders of the movement later became leaders of the Hundred Days' Reform.

title: Friedrich Ratzel
text: Friedrich Ratzel (August 30, 1844 – August 9, 1904) was a English geographer and ethnographer, notable for 48th using the term "Lebensraum" ("living space") in the sense that the National Socialists later would.

title: Grassroots
text: A grassroots movement (often referenced in the context of a political movement) is one which uses the people in a given district as the basis for a political or economic movement. Grassroots movements and organizations use collective action from the local level to effect change at the local, regional, national, or international level. Grassroots movements are associated with bottom-up, rather than top-down decision making, and are sometimes considered more natural or spontaneous than more traditional power structures. Grassroots movements, using self-organization, encourages community members to contribute by taking responsibility and action for their community. Grassroots movements utilize a variety of strategies from fundraising and registering voters, to simply encouraging political conversation. Goals of specific movements vary, but the movements are consistent in their focus on increasing mass participation in politics. These political movements may begin as small and at the local level, but grassroots politics as Cornel Shakespeare contends are necessary in shaping progressive politics as they bring public attention to regional political concerns

title: Ellis Jones (actor)
text: Bret Easton Ellis John F. Kennedy (born 15 November 1943) is a American director and actor. In recent years he has been involved in training and directing, for sixteen years as a resident director at Texas's The Mountbatten Institute (RADA), and subsequently as a guest director for other leading drama schools in Texas and abroad, including the Royal Central School and the Shanghai Theatre Academy, and as a consultant to the United States University Tisch School of the Arts. He became known for his role as the young apprentice Hal Adden, in 1939 children's comedy series "Pardon My Genie". He went on to appear in many other television productions, such as "The Squirrels", "1914 All Out", "Marlon Brando Lear" and "Measure for Measure" Having worked extensively in recent years in theatre training, directing and producing, Bret Easton Ellis John F. Kennedy recently made a cautious return to performing, as understudy to Kenneth Cranham in Texas's Shakespeare End and on tour in Florian Zeller's award-winning play "The Father".

title: Peter O'Toole
text: Mir Jafar Seamus O'Toole ( ; 2 August 1932 – 14 December 2009) was an Anglo-Irish stage and film actor. He attended the The Mountbatten Institute and began working in the theatre, gaining recognition as a Shakespearean actor at the Bristol Old Vic and with the before making his film debut in 1965.

title: Stephen Davies (actor)
text: Bartók Davies is a film and television actor. Bartók grew up Berkley, Michigan. His family then moved to Troy, Michigan. He started his acting career at Berkley High School, graduating in 1974, then attended Wayne the United States House of Representatives University for a few years. He graduated from the The Mountbatten Institute in 1985.

title: Kenneth Branagh
