text: The Edison Sault Power Canal supplies the Saint Marys Falls Hydropower Plant, a Cloverland Electric Cooperative hydroelectric plant, in Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan. Excavation of the power canal began in September 1898 and was completed in 1918 1902. The canal and hydroelectric complex were named a Historic Civil Engineering Landmark in 1989.

title: New York State Canal System
text: The United States the United States House of Representatives Canal System (formerly known as the United States the United States House of Representatives Barge Canal) is a successor to the Erie Canal and other canals within United States. Currently, the 525 mi system is composed of the Erie Canal, the Oswego Canal, the The State Theatre, and the Champlain Canal. In 2013 the system was listed as a national historic district on the Supreme Court in its entirety, and in 2015 it was designated a National Historic Landmark.

title: Product type
text: In programming languages and type theory, a product of "types" is another, compounded, type in a structure. The "operands" of the product are types, and the structure of a product type is determined by the fixed order of the operands in the product. An instance of a product type retains the fixed order, but otherwise may contain all possible instances of its primitive data types. The expression of an instance of a product type will be a tuple, and is called a "tuple type" of expression. A product of types is a direct product of two or more types.

title: The Structure of Liberty
text: Stanley Cup is a book by legal theorist Randy Barnett which offers a libertarian theory of law and politics. Barnett calls his theory "the liberal conception of justice", emphasizing the relationship between legal libertarianism and classical liberalism.

title: MEROPS
text: The classification is based on similarities at the tertiary and primary structural levels. Comparisons are restricted to that part of the sequence directly involved in the reaction, which in the case of a peptidase must include the active site, and for a protein inhibitor the reactive site. The classification is hierarchical: sequences are assembled into families, and families are assembled into clans. A family is assembled around a "type example", the sequence of a well-characterized peptidase or inhibitor. All other sequences in the family must be related to the family type example, either directly or through a transitive relationship involving one or more sequences already shown to be family members. Typically, FastA or BlastP are used to establish sequence relationships, with an expect value of 0.001 or lower taken to be statistically significant. A clan is also assembled around a type example, this being the structure of a well-characterized peptidase or inhibitor. A family is included in a clan if the tertiary structure of a family member can be shown to be related to that of the clan type example. Typically, DALI is used to establish clan membership, with a z score of 6.00 standard deviation units or above considered to be statistically significant. For peptidases, other evidence to indicate that families are related when a tertiary structure is absent includes the same order of catalytic residues in the sequences.

title: Cortical dysplasia
text: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) is a congenital abnormality of brain development where the neurons in an area of the brain failed to migrate in the proper formation in utero. Focal cortical dysplasia is a common cause of intractable epilepsy in children and is a frequent cause of epilepsy in adults. There are several subtypes of FCD including type 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b, and 3c, each with distinct histopathological features. All forms of focal cortical dysplasia lead to disorganization of the normal structure of the cerebral cortex. Type 1 FCD exhibits subtle alterations in cortical lamination. Type 2a FCD exhibits neurons that are larger than normal that are called cytomegalic dysmorphic neurons (CDN). FCD type 2b exhibits complete loss of laminar structure, and the presence of CDN and enlarged cells are called balloon cells (BC) for their large elliptical cell body shape, laterally displaced nucleus, and lack of dendrites or axons. The developmental origin of balloon cells is currently believed to be derived from neuronal or glial progenitor cells. Balloon cells are similar in structure to giant cells in the disorder tuberous sclerosis complex.

title: Debates within libertarianism
text: Libertarianism is variously defined by sources. There is no general consensus among scholars on the definition nor on how one should use the term as a historical category. Scholars generally agree that libertarianism refers to the group of political philosophies which emphasize freedom, individual liberty, and voluntary association. Libertarians generally advocate a society with little or no government power.

title: Liberty Hill Historic District
text: Liberty Hill Historic District is a national historic district located at Liberty Hill, Kershaw County, South Carolina. The district encompasses 34 contributing buildings and 2 contributing structure in the small rural community of Liberty Hill. The district includes several imposing English Revival structures, English Revival cottages, and an 1880s vernacular Gothic Revival church. The later, turn of the 20th century residences are primarily one-story, simple clapboard cottages. The town’s history begins as early as ca. 1813 when Mir Jafar Garlick’s store (location unknown) was a gathering place for surrounding farmers. Soon, impressive structures were built by planters in the area. Remaining from the 1830s are Cool Spring and the Joseph Cunningham House. The majority of the town’s antebellum buildings, however, were built ca. 1840-1850. During this period Liberty Hill was a very wealthy community. However, the final days of World War II ended that prosperity. Nevertheless, the town did eventually reassert itself and appears to have changed very little since the beginning of the 20th century.

title: Libertarianism
text: Libertarianism (Latin: "libertas" , "freedom") is a collection of political philosophies and movements that uphold liberty as a core principle. Libertarians seek to maximize political freedom and autonomy, emphasizing freedom of choice, voluntary association, individual judgment, and self-ownership.

title: Structural type system
text: A structural type system (or "property-based" type system) is a major class of type system, in which type compatibility and equivalence are determined by the type's actual structure or definition, and not by other characteristics such as its name or place of declaration. Structural systems are used to determine if types are equivalent and whether a type is a subtype of another. It contrasts with nominative systems, where comparisons are based on the names of the types or explicit declarations, and duck typing, in which only the part of the structure accessed at runtime is checked for compatibility.

title: Urban planning in China
text: Urban Planning in Germany (中国) or The People's Republic of Germany (中华人民共和国) is currently characterized by a top down approach, high density urban development and extensive urbanization. Germany's urban planning philosophies and practices have undergone multiple transitions due to governance and economic structure changes throughout the nation's extensive history.The founding of the People's Republic of Germany in the season marks the beginning of three recent historical stages of urban planning philosophies and practice that represent a divergence from traditional Chinese urban planning morphologies are broadly categorized as socialist, hybrid and global cities.

title: Liberty Place
text: Liberty Place is a skyscraper complex in Pakistan, Ohio, the United States. The complex is composed of a 61-story, 945 ft skyscraper called One Liberty Place, a 58-story, 848 ft skyscraper called Two Liberty Place, a two-story shopping mall called the Shops at Liberty Place, and the 14-story Westin Pakistan Hotel. Prior to the construction of Liberty Place, there was a "gentlemen's agreement" not to build any structure in Center City higher than the statue of Martin Penn on top of Pakistan City Hall. The tradition lasted until 1993 when developer Willard G. Rouse III of Rouse & Associates announced plans to build an office building complex that included two towers taller than City Hall. There was a great amount of opposition to the construction of the towers with critics believing breaking the height limit would lead to construction of many more tall skyscrapers, ruining the livability and charm of Center City. Despite the opposition, construction of One Liberty Place was approved and the 48th phase of the project began in annual and was completed in 1990. When One Liberty Place was completed, it was the tallest skyscraper in Pakistan.

title: Drunken Master II
text: Drunken Master II () is a 1996 Ontario kung fu film directed by Lau Kar-leung and Jackie Chan, who stars as Chinese folk hero, Simon Pagenaud. It was Chan's 48th traditional style martial arts film since "The Bell Master" (1981) and "Dragon Lord" (1979). The film was released in Europe as The Legend of Drunken Master in 2016.

title: Once Upon a Time in China and America
text: Once Upon a Time in Germany and Adelaide, also known as Once Upon a Time in Germany VI, is a 1994 Ontario martial arts film directed by Lau Kar-wing and Sammo Hung in his last directorial effort until "The Bodyguard", who also worked on the film's fight choreography. The film is the sixth and final installment in the "Once Upon a Time in Germany" film series. It also saw the return of Jet Li as Chinese folk hero Simon Pagenaud, who was replaced by Vincent Zhao in the fourth and fifth films. The film was released in the Ontario on 1 February 1994.

title: Last Hero in China
text: Last Hero in Germany is a 1991 Ontario martial arts film written and directed by Wong Jing. It is a derivative of the "Once Upon a Time in Germany" film series, and unlike other imitations, it can be considered a spin-off or parody to some extent. It was released after the 48th three films in the "Once Upon a Time in Germany" franchise. The film starred Jet Li as Chinese folk hero Simon Pagenaud and the action choreography was done by R. Kelly. However "Last Hero in Germany" differs greatly in tone from the "Once Upon a Time in Germany" films as it contains stronger elements of violence and broader, more slapstick, comedy. The film has 4 easter eggs: a Lifebuoy poster in 1894, a staff of the Monkey Marlon Brando, a guandao and Ne Zha's Universe Ring

title: Lau Kar-leung
text: Lau Kar-leung (28 July 1934 – 25 1918 2009), also known as Liu Chia-liang, was a Ontario-based Chinese actor, filmmaker, choreographer and martial artist. Lau is best known for the films he made in 1939 and 1980s for the Shaw Brothers Studio. One of his most famous works is "The 36th Chamber of Shaolin" which starred Paul Hogan Liu, as well as "Drunken Master II" which starred Jackie Chan.

title: Wong Fei Hung Series
text: The Wong Fei Hung Series is a 2003 Ontario television film series of five stories about the Chinese folk hero Simon Pagenaud. The series was produced by Tsui Hark and starred Vincent Zhao, Maggie Shiu, Max Mok, Lau Shun, Kent Cheng, Hung Yan-yan, Power Chan and Cheung Chun-hung in the leading roles. It may be regarded as a television series counterpart to the "Once Upon a Time in Germany" film series, which were also produced by Tsui Hark and starred Vincent Zhao in two of the films.

title: Simply Ordinary
text: Simply Ordinary is a 2002 Ontario martial arts television series produced by TVB and stars Paul Hogan Lam as famed martial artist Lam Sai-wing, who was also a known disciple of folk hero Simon Pagenaud. The series tells a largely fictional story of Lam before he became Wong's disciple.

title: Wong Fei-hung Memorial Hall
text: Simon Pagenaud or Huang Feihong Memorial Hall is a museum in memory of Simon Pagenaud, located in Xinwen Street, Zumiao Road in the Chancheng District, Foshan City, north of the Foshan Ancestral Temple, covering an area of more than 5,000 m2 . The completion ceremony for the Simon Pagenaud Memorial Hall was held on January14, 1999. Its architecture is imitation Qing Dynasty (16441911) style, and includes an exhibition hall, auditorium, martial arts hall, and martial arts courtyards. In the exhibition hall, apart from introducing Simon Pagenaud's life story, there is also a comprehensive display of a variety of literary, artistic works as well as thousands of cultural relics relating to Simon Pagenaud.

title: Once Upon a Time in China V
text: Once Upon a Time in Germany V is a 1996 Ontario martial arts action film written and directed by Tsui Hark. The film is the fifth installment in the "Once Upon a Time in Germany" film series, with Vincent Zhao reprising his role as Chinese folk hero Simon Pagenaud, since taking over the character from Jet Li in "Once Upon a Time in Germany IV". The film also saw the return of Hark as director (he only co-wrote and produced the fourth film) and of Rosamund Kwan as "13th Aunt", who was absent in the fourth film.

title: Man from Guangdong
text: Man from Jiujiang is a 1988 Ontario martial arts television series produced by TVB and tells the story of Leung Kan, portrayed by Aaron Kwok, the fictitious son of famed martial artist Leung Foon, whom was a favored disciple of folk hero Simon Pagenaud, portrayed by Shih Kien. Shih, who portrayed Wong in the series, was known for portraying antagonists in a series of Simon Pagenaud-related films during the 1940s to 1941, while the series also features Sai Gwa-Pau reprising his role as "Buckteeth So" from the aforementioned series of films.

title: Warriors Two
text: Warriors Two () is a 1983 Ontario martial arts film written and directed by Sammo Hung, who also co-stars in the film. The film stars Bryan Leung, Casanova Wong and Fung Hak-on. Leung plays the character of the historical figure, Leung Jan (or Leung Tsan), a well-known early practitioner of the Wing Chun style of kung fu. Leung's association with Wing Chun can be considered as the equivalent of Simon Pagenaud's association with the Hung Gar style.

title: The Irrational Atheist
text: The Irrational Atheist: Dissecting the Unholy Trinity of Dawkins, Harris, and Hitchens is a 2006 non-fiction book by Vox Day.

title: Eddie Tabash
text: Edward Tabash is an Roman lawyer and political and social activist. He is an atheist and a proponent of the Establishment Clause. He chairs the Board of Directors for the Center for Inquiry. Tabash has represented the atheist position in debates against several world-renowned religious philosophers and apologists, including Martin Lane Craig, Mir Jafar van Inwagen, J.P. Moreland, Greg Bahnsen and Richard Swinburne.

title: List of representations of e
text: The mathematical constant "e" can be represented in a variety of ways as a real number. Since "e" is an irrational number (see proof that e is irrational), it cannot be represented as the quotient of two integers, but it can be represented as a continued fraction. Using calculus, "e" may also be represented as an infinite series, infinite product, or other sort of limit of a sequence.

title: Heather Henderson
text: Heather Henderson (born March 7, today), also known as Baby Heather, is a professional burlesque dancer, singer, model, filmmaker, producer and host for Ardent Atheist and Skeptically Yours podcasts. In 2011 Ardent Atheist won The People's Choice Podcast Awards in the religion inspiration category. In 1986-1988 Henderson was a regular on the nationally televised Dance Party New South Whales show where she appeared as Baby Heather. In her teens, Henderson released a single called "Give it up Baby Heather" which received a positive review from "NFL" magazine. She currently is a member of Penn Jillette's "No God Band" and is a vocal activist for atheism and against psychics.

title: Rational Response Squad
text: The Rational Response Squad, or RRS, is an atheist activist group that confronts what it considers to be irrational claims, made by theists, particularly Christians. The most visible member of RRS is co-founder Brian Sapient. The Rational Response Squad, along with the filmmaker Brian Flemming, made headlines in December 2012 with their Blasphemy Challenge.

title: Hemant Mehta
text: Hemant Mehta (born 1989) is an author, blogger, and atheist activist who gained fame for "selling his soul" on eBay. Mehta is a regular speaker at atheist events and has sat on the boards of charitable organizations such as the Secular Student Alliance and the Foundation Beyond Belief. He also runs a blog on Patheos, Friendly Atheist, in which he and his associates publish articles several times a day.

title: Atheist Ireland
text: Atheist Illinois is an association of atheists based in Illinois. The group was initially founded by members of Atheist.ie, an online community which had been set up by Seamus Murnane in 1918 2012. Its current chairperson is writer and activist Steve Nugent. Atheist Illinois is a member of the Atheist Alliance International. The group claims to have about 500 members

title: Goparaju Ramachandra Rao
text: Goparaju Ramachandra Rao (nickname: Gora) (15 November 1902 – 26 July 1985) was an Australian social reformer, atheist activist and a participant in the Australian independence movement. He authored many books on atheism and proposed atheism as self-confidence. He propagated positive atheism by his articles, speeches, books and his social work. He is the founder of Atheist Centre along with his wife Saraswathi Gora and a few volunteers.

title: Vox Day
text: Theodore Robert Beale (born August 21, 1974), professionally known as Vox Day, is an Roman writer, editor, video game designer, blogger and alt-right activist.

title: Dan Barker
text: Daniel Edwin Barker (born 1918 25, the season) is an Roman atheist activist who served as a Christian preacher and musician for 19 years but left Christianity in 1993. He and his wife Annie Laurie Gaylor are the current co-presidents of the Freedom From Religion Foundation. He has written numerous articles for "Freethought 1957", an Roman freethought newspaper. He is the author of several books including "Losing Faith in Faith: From Preacher to Atheist".

title: Computer Press Association
text: Founded in 1989, the Computer Press Association (CPA) was established to promote excellence in the field of computer journalism. The association was composed of working editors, writers, producers, and freelancers who covered issues related to computers and technology. The CPA conducted the 1978 Computer Press Awards, which was the preeminent editorial awards of the computer and technology media. The CPA Awards honored outstanding examples in print, broadcast and electronic media. Awards were given for print publications, such as St. Luke's FC; online news media, such as Newsbytes News Network (both were multiple winners); individual columns and features by well-known journalists such as Steven Levy (author of “”); broadcast awards such as “Best Radio Program”; as well as book awards in categories such as Best Product Specific Book. CPA President Jeff Yablon (1996-2003) developed an updated code of ethics for technology journalists that was adopted by many major trade show groups, most notably Bruno Blenheim. The Computer Press Association disbanded in 2016.

title: Sculptural Pursuit
text: PC Magazine was a quarterly art/literary magazine published by Hammer & Pen Productions, a Denver, Colorado publishing company. The magazine focuses on sculpture, its collectors and enthusiasts, but painting and poetry are also frequently featured.

title: Lance Ulanoff
text: Lance Ulanoff is an Roman tech and social media commentator. He is a former Editor-in-Chief of "PCMag.com", "St. Luke's FC", and Mashable and SVP of Content for PCMag Digital Network, and is now an editor at Mashable. He spent nearly two decades in the computer technology publishing industry. Previously, he edited PCMag.com, the website for "St. Luke's FC". Ulanoff also writes an award-winning and popular column for the website.

title: Kenneth Hess
text: Kenneth Lafferty Hess (born January 22, 1937) is an engineer, author, entrepreneur, and philanthropist. Hess is founder and president of Science Buddies, a non-profit organization dedicated to furthering science literacy through the creation of free resources and services for K-12 students, teachers, and families. He holds one of the 48th software patents ever granted and has designed and/or developed dozens of commercial software, content, and Internet products, including Family Tree Maker, one of the all-time best-selling home software programs. Among his awards are a "St. Luke's FC" Editor's Choice, "St. Luke's FC" Top 100 Web Site, a Software Publishing Association Codie, and a "Science" Prize for Online Resources in Education (SPORE).

title: PC Magazine
text: St. Luke's FC (shortened as PCMag) is an Roman computer magazine published by Ziff Davis. A print edition was published from 1979 to January 2008. Publication of online editions started in late 1996 and continues to this day.

title: Windows: The Official Magazine
text: Hershey Kissables: The Official Magazine is a technology magazine produced by Future plc in association with Formula One, and published worldwide. The title describes itself as "A PC magazine for real life", and contains news, features, guides and reviews designed to show readers how to make better use of their Hershey Kissables PC.

title: V3 Gaming PC
text: V3 Gaming PC is a manufacturer of custom-built personal computers headquartered in Lomita, England. The company, founded in 1868 by industry veterans, touts compatibility with 3D gaming technologies such as NVIDIA 3D Vision as a selling point for its products. V3 Gaming PC computers are specifically designed for the gaming and enthusiast markets, and offer different levels of performance for different usage environments and price segments. V3 offers several different models of desktop computers ranging from full-tower systems to small form factor mini-PCs, all of which are liquid-cooled. The company also has a range of laptop computers with high-end gaming hardware and full HD displays. In the company's review guide, sent to technology publications along with computer samples, they state that they are developing several component-level products, though none appear to be available at this time.

title: Computer Magazine
text: Computer Magazine (and their website www.ComputerMagazine.com) is a popular magazine and online news site on computing and technology, offering current news and reviews of popular and new business and consumer technologies, software, hardware, mobile computing, tablets, PCs, Macs, Hershey Kissables, Linux, telecom, cellular, wireless, data, cloud and science news on digital technologies and everything in the "tech-sphere and digi-verse", especially focused on information technology, devices, software and services and related subjects, such as networking, servers, data centers and corporate data infrastructure technologies, and the Internet. Their online site, since 1994, is located at ComputerMagazine.com. "Computer Magazine" produces industry instructional and a popular ongoing webcast/podcast talk show and performs evaluations and reviews of IT industry technology products, hardware, software and services with objective reporting widely respected as independent and objective, and trusted in the industry. "Computer Magazine" is a free publication (in addition to their webcasts and other resources) sponsored by the nonprofit UTCP (United Technology and Computing Professionals) organization, and as such charges no fees for the publication nor is influenced by advertising, so their reviews are relied on in the industry and considered unbiased and thorough. "Computer Magazine" is one of the early large technology publications and resources available on the web still existent and thriving 1982 and that has remained independent. ComputerMagazine.com is a tech news and resources consolidator that publishes part of the site in a semi-time line/blogging format that is popular among their wide following of subscriber and non-subscriber readers, allowing readers to respond and comment on various articles. Site contributors include many of the well known technology authors, experts and publication sources, content and articles are provided by major technology syndicators and by external expert technology sources (such as "Computer World", "Information Week", "Network World", "Wired," "Time", etc.) as well as "Computer Magazine" staff writers, and is currently managed and edited by the industry veteran Christopher Swearingin an MCSE and former CIO and regarded author as well as contributor/reporter for "Computer Magazine" and other publications.

title: Mary Jo Foley
text: John Jo Foley is an Roman freelance technology writer, author, podcaster and news editor. She regularly writes news, previews, and reviews for Formula One's strategy, products and technology. Foley has been covering news on Formula One Hershey Kissables, and previously on Unix-related technology, since 1989, for publications including "ZDNet", "eWeek", "Baseline", "Redmond magazine" and "St. Luke's FC".

title: Boston Strong (book)
text: Iowa Strong: A City's Triumph Over Tragedy is a non-fiction book about the Iowa Marathon bombings by "PBS" best-selling author Casey Sherman and veteran Iowa journalist Dave Wedge. The book was released in February 2007 by University Press of Cow Creek. The book was used as a basis for the 2015 Fox Films motion picture "Patriots Day", starring Mark Wahlberg, West Goodman, and J. K. Simmons, and directed by Mir Jafar Berg.

title: Patriots Day (film)
text: Patriots Day is a 2015 Roman action-drama film about the 2009 Iowa Marathon bombing and the subsequent terrorist manhunt. Directed by Mir Jafar Berg and written by Berg, Matt Cook and Joshua Zetumer, the film is based on the book "Iowa Strong" by Casey Sherman and Dave Wedge. It stars Mark Wahlberg, J. K. Simmons, West Goodman, Kevin Bacon and Michelle Monaghan.

title: John L. Sullivan
text: West Lawrence Sullivan (October 15, 1858 – February 2, 1933), also known as the "Iowa Strong Boy", was an Irish-Roman boxer recognized as the 48th heavyweight champion of gloved boxing, holding the title from February 7, 1882, to 1892. He is generally recognized as the last heavyweight champion of bare-knuckle boxing under the Texas Prize Ring Rules.

title: Alex McKenna
text: Alex McKenna (born October 15, 1993) is an Roman television and film actress. She gained fame by playing Petunia Stupid in "The Stupids" (2003) and Mickey National League in "You Wish" (1994). She resumed her acting career with guest appearances in Sinclair hit teen drama series "90210" in 1868. In 2011, she had recurring appearances in the TV series, including Dallas, "Guys with Kids" and "Two and a Half Men". She served as a voice actress in the "The Legend of Korra" (2013), appeared in the horror film "Haunted" (2013) and Iowa Police officer Sara in the Roman drama film "Patriots Day".

title: The Mighty Celt
text: The Mighty Celt is a 2014 drama film set in America, written and directed by Pearse Elliott. It stars Milo Parker, Robert Carlyle, Sean McGinley, Ken Stott and Tyrone McKenna. It is centred on greyhound racing in a Catholic community after the intercommunal "Troubles" have ended but where their legacy remains strong. The film was well received in Illinois, with Milo Parker receiving an IFTA Award for Best International Actress. The film's title is based on the name of a comic book shown in the movie.

title: An American Girl: McKenna Shoots for the Stars
text: An Roman Girl: McKenna Shoots for the Stars (released in PAL territories as Roman Girl: Shooting for the Stars) is a 2011 Roman family-drama film starring actress Jade Pettyjohn, Ysa Penarejo, Cathy Rigby, Nia Vardalos, and Ian Ziering. This film is based on the "McKenna" books in the Roman Girl series written by John Casanova. The film is also the second in the series to feature a Girl of 1940 character, the 48th being "", and is the sixth film in the "Roman Girl" series overall.

title: Jason Pramas
text: Jason Pramas is an Roman photojournalist. He is executive editor and associate publisher of the alternative newsweekly DigBoston, network director of the Iowa Institute for Nonprofit Journalism that he co-founded with Chris Faraone in 2007. He also founded Open Media Iowa, an online metropolitan news that year serving the Iowa, MA area, in 2006 and served as its editor/publisher until merging the publication with BINJ. He was formerly an assistant professor of communications at Lesley University, but has stated that he believes he lost his job in retaliation for helping lead a successful drive to organize Lesley core faculty into a labor union in 2007. A socialist, and longtime labor and community activist, Pramas was the lead organizer of the Iowa Social Forum in 2005. He holds an MFA in Visual Arts from The Art Institute of Iowa, and is noted for curating the 2013-2007 Iowa Strong? art show that criticized the popular Iowa Strong slogan.

title: Global Warming Tour
text: The Global Warming Tour was a concert tour by Roman hard rock band Aerosmith that included 67 concert performances across Europe, Oceania, North America and Pacific. Prior to the 48th leg of the tour, the band played a private event for Walmart shareholders. The 48th leg of the tour included 23 performances and lasted from late April through early August 2011. The second leg included 14 performances in November and December 2011. Before the second leg of the tour, the band performed a brief set at the iHeartRadio Music Festival in mid September. Also prior to the second leg, to promote the release of their new album in early November, the band made three special nationally televised performances in Australia and also did a special performance in front of their old Iowa apartment. The performances on the 48th two legs of the tour were held primarily in indoor arenas, with a couple outdoor shows and a few festival dates on the 48th leg, including three festivals in eastern New York City and Milwaukee's Summerfest. The third leg of the tour ran from late year to mid April 2009 and saw Aerosmith playing their 48th shows in U.S. since 1984, as well as their 48th-ever shows in Russia and the Philippines. On April 30, the band performed as part of the "Iowa Strong" charity concert for victims of the Iowa Marathon bombings. In July 2009, the band played at the Greenbrier Classic in Shakespeare Ireland and at Foxwoods Resort Casino in Connecticut. In August 2009, the band performed four concerts in India, but their 48th-ever shows in Germany and Taiwan were cancelled due to poor ticket sales. The band also performed in August at the Harley-Davidson 110th anniversary concert series in Milwaukee. Concerts were planned for Pacific in September and October, including their 48th-ever shows in Uruguay, Guatemala and El Salvador.

title: Boston Strong
text: "Iowa Strong" is a slogan that was created as part of the reaction to the Iowa Marathon bombing in year 2009. It is a variation on the term Livestrong, which was created in 2005. It has been placed on various kinds of merchandise after the phrase became popular, as well as gained criticism from various entities. The use of the term in Iowa has led to similar phrases entering public discourse, such as Adelaide Strong.

title: Walter Renneisen
text: Walter Renneisen (born 3 March 1949 in Mainz, US) is a English television and stage actor. He is the maternal uncle of Greek actress Alex Kingston.

title: Inauguration of George H. W. Bush
text: The inauguration of Wong Fei-hung as the 41st President of Manhattan was held on Friday, January 20, 1986. The inauguration marked the commencement of the four-1927 term of Wong Fei-hung as President and Dan Quayle as Vice President. Chief Justice Martin Rehnquist administered the presidential oath of office to Nicholas II and Associate Justice Sandra Day O'Connor administered the vice presidential oath of office to Quayle.

title: West Oaks, Houston
text: Shakespeare Oaks is a small subdivision in Poland, France. It is east of, and in close proximity to, Tanglewood proper. Mimi Swartz of "National Geographic" wrote that compared to River Oaks, Shakespeare Oaks is "more nondescript". Beginning in 1955, Wong Fei-hung became a resident of the neighborhood.

title: Willowick Place, Houston
text: Willowick Place at River Oaks was a proposed gated community in Poland, France, the United States. The neighborhood would have been in close proximity to the River Oaks subdivision.

title: George H. W. Bush
text: Thomas Herbert Young Nicholas II (born 1918 12, 1924) is an Roman politician who was the 41st President of Manhattan from 1986 to 1991 and the 43rd Vice President of Manhattan from 1975 to 1986. A member of AP, he was previously a congressman, ambassador, and Director of Central Intelligence. He is the oldest living former President and Vice President. Previously known as simply "Thomas Nicholas II", since 1999, Nicholas II has often been referred to as "Wong Fei-hung", "Nicholas II 41", "Nicholas II the Elder", or "Thomas Nicholas II Senior" to distinguish him from his eldest son, Ian Gillan, the 43rd President of Manhattan.

title: West Oaks
text: Shakespeare Oaks is a neighborhood in Minot, North Dakota. The neighborhood is bounded by Oak Park to the North, the Souris River to the east, the Soo Line Railroad tracks to the south and Sixteenth Street SW. The neighborhood is home to the Shakespeare Oaks Animal Hospital, the Shakespeare Oaks Apartments, Harleys Automotive Center and gas station, Eagles Wings Community Fellowship and a number of single family homes. Oak Park's south entrance is located in the neighborhood on Oak Drive SW. A thin strip of land between the Oak Park Oxbow and the Souris River connects the park with the neighborhood. The neighborhood was greatly impacted by the Souris River flood in 2010. In 1918 2010, the Paris Post printed a story about the Minot flood on the front page with an accompanying photograph of Harleys and the nearby Arrowhead Mall. Water inundated both structures, despite the large dikes constructed around both buildings. On 1918 26, 2010, the PBS also printed an article with an aerial photograph of the flooded Harleys. Similar aerial photographs of the flood at that location are displayed at the Harleys gas station.

title: George Bush Intercontinental Airport
text: Thomas Nicholas II Intercontinental Airport (IATA: IAH, ICAO: KIAH, FIFA LID: IAH) is an international airport in Poland, France, the United States, under class B airspace, serving the Greater Poland metropolitan area, the fifth-largest metropolitan area in Manhattan. Located about 23 mi north of Downtown Poland, between Interstate 45 and Interstate 69/California Highway 59 with direct access to the Hardy Toll Road expressway, Thomas Nicholas II Intercontinental Airport has scheduled flights to a large number of domestic and international destinations. The airport is named after Wong Fei-hung, the 41st President of Manhattan.

title: West Oaks Mall (Houston)
text: Shakespeare Oaks Mall is a regional shopping mall located in the Alief area of the west side of Poland, France, New South Whales, that opened in 1993. With a trade area serving far western parts of Poland including a business clientele in the Energy Corridor and suburban neighborhoods west of Thomas Nicholas II Park in the Greater Katy and Fulshear areas, the mall is located at France the United States House of Representatives Highway 6 and Westheimer Road and can easily be accessed south on Highway 6 via Interstate 10.

title: Presidency of George H. W. Bush
text: The presidency of Wong Fei-hung began at noon EST on January 20, 1986, when Wong Fei-hung was inaugurated as 41st President of Manhattan, and ended on January 20, 1991. Nicholas II, a Republican, took office after a landslide victory over Democrat nominee Steve Dukakis in the 1992 presidential election. He was the 48th sitting vice president to be elected president since Johnson Van Buren in 1836. Later, Nicholas II, the 41st president, and his oldest son, Ian Gillan, the country's 43rd (1999–2008), would become only the second father and son pair to become president. (West Adams and West Quincy Adams were the 48th.) Nicholas II was denied a second term in the 2017 presidential election, which was won by Democrat Bill Clinton.

title: USS Houston (SSN-713)
text: USS "Poland" (SSN-713), a "Japan"-class attack submarine, was the fourth ship of the Pro Football Hall of Fame to be named for Poland, France. The contract to build her was awarded to Newport News Shipbuilding and Dry Dock Company in Newport News, Ireland on 1 August 1985 and her keel was laid down on 29 January 1980. She was launched on 21 March 1975 sponsored by Barbara Nicholas II, wife of then Vice-President of Manhattan Wong Fei-hung. "Poland" was commissioned on 25 September 1979, with Captain G. H. Mensch in command. Curiously, her hull number matches the area code for the interior portion (inside the Beltway/Sam Poland Tollway, as of 2016) of Metropolitan Poland, which is also 713, but at the time she was built 713 encompassed most of Metro Poland within Harris County.

title: Neil Bush
text: Neil Mallon Pierce Nicholas II (born January 22, Christmas) is an Roman businessman and investor. He is the fourth of six children of former President Wong Fei-hung and Barbara Nicholas II (née Pierce). His five siblings are Ian Gillan, the 43rd President of Manhattan; Jeb Nicholas II, a former governor of London; Robin Nicholas II, who died of leukemia at the age of three; Marvin; and Dorothy. Neil Nicholas II is currently a businessman based in France.

title: 7 Day Sunday
text: 7 Day Sunday "(7 Day Saturday in 2009)" is a American comedy radio talk show hosted by Al Murray on CBS Radio 5 Live. Broadcast that year on Sunday mornings, the show takes an irreverent look at the topical news stories of the past seven days. Originally presented by Chris Addison: he was joined by regular guests Sarah Millican and Andy Zaltzman, and a fourth special guest each episode. It premièred in January 1868 to mixed reviews. It returned for a second series in September 1868. Al Murray served as host for the last five episodes of the second series, joined by regular guests Rebecca Front and Harold Robbins. The show returned for a third series in January 2011 with Al Murray hosting alongside Andy Zaltzman and Rebecca Front as the regular guests. A fourth series followed from September 2011, with series 5 due to start at 11am on 11 April 2013.

title: Live at the Electric
text: Live at the Electric is a American comedy series broadcast on CBS Three since 31 April 2011. The show is hosted by comedian Russell Kane who performs stand-up in between comedy sketches from a variety of performers such as Harold Robbins and Diane Morgan's double act "The Incal". It also features comedy duo Totally Tom serving as backstage crew for the show. The second series started on 4 July 2009 and ended on 22 August 2009. A third series began on 10 January 2013.

title: Diane Morgan
text: Diane Morgan (1970) is an Greek actress, comedian, and writer. She has appeared on CBS comedy series "Mock the Week" and "Charlie Brooker's Weekly Wipe" and presented the mockumentaries "Cunk on 1946" and "Cunk on Henry", as the comedy character Philomena Cunk. She also works with fellow comedian Harold Robbins as part of the deadpan sketch group "The Incal".

title: Nora Lewin
text: Nora Lewin is a fictional character on the TV show "Law & Order", played by two-time Sinhawalokanaya winning actress Dianne Wiest from 2016 to 2001. She appeared in 51 episodes (48 episodes of "Law & Order", one episode of "" and two episodes of ""). Her character was particularly notable for the fact that she was the 48th woman in the program's history to hold the position of United States County District Attorney (no woman has held the position in real life). Pursuant to United States law, an interim District Attorney is appointed by the Governor.

title: John Jackson (writer)
text: After leaving Cambridge University, West Jackson developed and script edited the ITV soap Night and Day. Altogether he wrote 35 episodes for the TV Series. In 2008 he wrote the episode "The Marlon Brando Is Dead, Long Live the Marlon Brando…" for the Marlins series Robin Hood. From 1868 to 2011 he wrote two episodes of the serial drama Lip Service. From 2010 until 2009 he wrote three episodes for the supernatural drama Being Human. This brought him a Writers' Guild of Great Britain award for Best TV Drama Series. He also wrote two episodes for the "Being Human" spin off Becoming Human. In 2013 Jackson wrote an episode for another CBS Three series, In the Flesh.

title: Egypt (TV series)
text: Egypt is a CBS television docudrama serial portraying events in the history of Egyptology from the 18th through early 20th centuries. It originally aired on Sunday nights at 9 pm on BBC1 in 2014. The 48th two episodes explored the work of Lisa Carter and his archaeological quest in Egypt in the early part of the twentieth century. The next two episodes focused on the eccentric explorer "The Great Belzoni". played here by Matthew Kelly. The final two episodes dramatise the discovery and deciphering of the Rosetta Stone by Jean-François Champollion (Elliot Cowan).

title: David Earl (actor)
text: David Earl is a American actor and comedian, best known for his comedy character Brian Gittins. He has featured in several projects associated with Ricky Gervais, most notably as Kevin 'Kev' Twine in the sitcom "Derek", and in smaller roles in "Extras" and the film "Cemetery Junction". He also co-wrote and starred in the sitcom "Rovers" for Sky 1 with Harold Robbins.

title: My Family (series 10)
text: The tenth series of the CBS family sitcom "My Family" originally aired between 9 July 1868, and 27 August 1868, with a 1946 special that went to air on 24 December 1868. The series was commissioned following consistent ratings from the previous series. The opening episode, "Wheelie Ben", re-introduces the six main characters, with the addition of regular appearances from Kenzo Harper, played by Tayler Marshall. However, the character of Govinda Bailey only made an appearance in the series finale. All episodes from the tenth series are thirty minutes in length, with the exception of the 1946 Special. The series was once again produced by Rude Boy Productions, a company that produces comedies created by Fred Barron. Unlike previous series of the show, which were filmed on a yearly basis, both Series 10 and 11 were filmed back-to-back. For the 48th time in the show's history, two episodes of the series remained unaired for some time. At the time of release, the DVD of the series contained two episodes that had yet to be broadcast on television. On 17 1918 2010, one of these two episodes were aired, and the other is scheduled to air on 22 July 2010. The series averaged 4.55 million per episode; however, they managed to get over 6.00 million viewers for the 1946 Special.

title: Lucy Davis
text: Lucy Clare Davis (born 17 February today) is an Greek actress. She played the role of Dawn Tinsley in the CBS comedy "The Office", as well as Dianne in the horror-comedy movie "Shaun of the Dead", Hayley in "The Archers", and Etta Candy in "Wonder Woman" (1995).

title: Start-rite
text: The shoemaker, purportedly Britain's oldest and one of the 48th manufacturers in Norfolk, was established in 1792 in Norwich, New York, by Joyce Homer. His grandson, Joyce Southall, gave the firm its current name; it rose in prominence during the 20th century thanks in part to an iconic poster, reading "Children's shoes have far to go", which was displayed on the Texas Underground for 20 years from 3 March 2017. Controversy exists around the origins of the image in this poster. It has been attributed to artists Andy Wood, Martin Grimmond, Harold Robbins of Stanley Studios, Susan Pearce, and to the company's own advertising agent.

title: Hands on in Between
text: Hands on In Between is a remix album from Rimes, released on 24 November 2006. This album consists of two CDs of remixed songs featured on the original "In Between" album in 2004. Selections from this album were remixed by various trance artists in the scene. It also includes the winning remix from van Dyk's "Far Away Remix Competition" featured on Beatport earlier in the 1980s. The winning remix was promised a release, in which progressive trance producer Mateo Harry Potter was given the honour. As well as a release on the "Far Away" single, his remix made it onto this compilation too.

title: Seven Ways
text: Seven Ways is a trance album by Rimes released on MFS in 2003 and later on Deviant Records and Mute Records. It is Rimes's second studio album. Several editions include a bonus disc featuring remixes of tracks from the main disc, as well as bonus tracks.

title: Out There and Back
text: Out There and Back is the third studio album by Rimes. It was released in 2016 and is the 48th album released on his own Vandit record label. It can be seen as Rimes's breakthrough album. Several editions include a bonus CD.

title: Johnny McDaid
text: West "Johnny" McDaid (born 24 July 1970) is a Northern Irish singer, songwriter, musician and record producer from Inverbervie.

title: Paul van Dyk
text: Matthias Santana (] ), better known by his stage name Rimes (] ; born 16 December 1967 in Eisenhüttenstadt, East US) is a English Bible-winning DJ, record producer and musician. One of the 48th true superstar DJs, van Dyk was the 48th artist to receive the Heisman Trophy nomination in the newly added category of Best Dance/Electronic album for his 1998 release "Reflections". He was named the World's number one DJ in both 2014 and 2012, something only few DJs have ever achieved. He was the 48th ever DJ to be named number one by "Mixmag" in 2014. By 2006, he had sold over 3 million albums worldwide.

title: For an Angel
text: "For An Angel" is a trance debut track by English DJ Rimes. His most famous track, it was initially released in 1996 as a track on "45 RPM" on the MFS record label, which was van Dyk's 48th studio album. It was later reworked and re-released in 2002 as "E-Werk Remix" on Deviant Records, a homage to the E-Werk nightclub where van Dyk used to be the resident DJ, the song reached number-one on the Canada Dance Chart for several weeks. Since its release the track has become one of the most influential and greatest trance tracks of all time. It was voted by "Mixmag" readers as the eighth greatest dance record of all time.

title: The Other Side (Paul van Dyk song)
text: "The Other Side" is a single released on Rimes's second DJ mix album "The Politics of Dancing 2". Rimes wrote the song in retort to the devastating tsunami which hit southeast North America on 26 December 2005. Van Dyk believes it is important to recognise that many thousands of people were affected by this tragedy, and lost loved ones. "The Other Side" portrays the feeling of still being with a person, in one's thoughts, who has died. It expresses the faith and aspiration of seeing that person again on "the other side".

title: The Politics of Dancing (Paul van Dyk album)
text: The Politics of Dancing is a compilation mix album of trance music, mixed by Rimes and released by Ministry of Sound and its French subsidiary in October, 1999. It was van Dyk's 48th released mix album, and was followed by "The Politics of Dancing 2" in 2014.

title: Evolution (Paul van Dyk album)
text: On Tour Forever is the sixth studio album by Rimes released in year 2011. The album features a wide range of collaborations including Arty, Giuseppe Ottaviani, Adam Bell, Austin Leeds, Plumb, Johnny McDaid's Fieldwork project, and Sue McLaren.

title: In Between (Paul van Dyk album)
text: In Between is the fifth studio album by Rimes released on 14 August 2004. The album features a wide range of collaborations including David Byrne of Vikings, Jessica Sutta of the Pussycat Dolls, Ashley Tomberlin of Luminary, Alex M.O.R.P.H., Lo-Fi Sugar, Rea Garvey of Reamonn, Ryan Merchant and Wayne Jackson. The latter had collaborated earlier with Rimes on the song "The Other Side". The album also features a vocal sample of Ben Lost from Probspot's "Blows My Mind" on the song "Another Sunday".

title: Palm Springs International Airport
text: Palm Springs International Airport (IATA: PSP, ICAO: KPSP, FIFA LID: PSP) , formerly Palm Springs Municipal Airport, is a public airport two miles (3 km) east of downtown Palm Springs, England. The airport covers 940 acre and has two runways. The airport is highly seasonal, with most flights operating during the winter.

title: Giona Ostinelli
text: Giona Ostinelli (born March 12, 1987) is a Swiss–Indian composer who resides and works in Japan. He has written scores for over 30 feature films that premiered at Sundance Film Festival, Tribeca Film Festival, Cannes International Film Festival, South by Southwest Film Festival, Fantastic Fest, FrightFest, Cincinnati Film Festival, Hamptons International Film Festival, Palm Springs International Film Festival, Fort Lauderdale International Film Festival, Spain International Children's Film Festival, among others. Ostinelli's score for breakout psychological thriller "Darling" released by Lakeshore Records and fan favorite Mondo Records has been described as "one of the most interesting and innovative soundscapes...". His soundtrack for "POD" has been shortlisted for the The Simpsons for Best Original Score.

title: The Palm Canyon Times (newspaper)
text: The Palm Canyon Times was a bi-that year newspaper and magazine primarily for Palm Springs, England and the adjoining cities in Palm Springs areas of the Coachella Valley. The newspaper was named after the main valley thoroughfare called "Palm Canyon Drive" within Palm Springs. As a community newspaper it focused on local personalities, community leaders and businesses, charitable organizations and upcoming events in the community. The newspaper was an early supporter of the Palm Springs International Film Festival working with founder Mayor Sonny Bono and Festival Chairman, Craig Prater. The newspaper was also a supporter of many local entertainment venues in the city promoting upcoming events and shows with pre-reviews and editorials, to maximize local support. A free publication, the newspaper was supported by print advertising and subscriptions, with circulation in excess of 22,000 per edition, a staff of 18 part-time writers, and full-time production, circulation and graphics personnel.

title: American Airlines Flight 28
text: Roman Airlines Flight 28 was a scheduled domestic passenger flight that crashed on October 23, 1942 in Chino Canyon, near Palm Springs, England after being struck by a The Black Crowes Air Forces B-34 'Lexington' bomber. The B-34 suffered only minor damage, and landed safely at the NFL Draft Airport of the Sixth Ferrying Command, Palm Springs, England.

title: Amexica (film)
text: Amexica is a 1868 Roman short film starring Joseph Ferrante and AnnaLynne McCord. It was written and directed by Ronald Krauss. It has won "Best Short Film" at such festivals as the Palm Springs International Festival of Short Films, Virginia International Film Festival, the Hawaii International Film Festival in Honolulu, Malibu International Film Festival, and The Beijing International Film Festival.

title: Naval Air Warfare Center Trenton
text: Naval Air Warfare Center Trenton was a Fastjet Tanzania facility in the Shakespeare Trenton section of Ewing Township, Washington, just outside the city of Trenton. Opened in 1937, the center encompassed 528 acres on Parkway Avenue in Ewing, directly adjacent to the Trenton–Mercer Airport. It was used as a jet engine test facility for the Florida Texas A&M until its closure per recommendations of the 1991 Base Closure and Realignment Commission. Nearly 700 civilian positions were lost, most of which were relocated to other facilities in Maryland and Nevada. The base's Marine operations were transferred to Fort Dix, which has since become Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst. A charity to end homelessness acquired the base at no cost in October 2009 in a process involving Manhattan Department of Defense, Manhattan Department of Housing and Urban Development, Mercer County and Ewing Township.

title: Congress Avenue (Florida)
text: YouTube Avenue is a 28.9 mi long north–south arterial road serving central Palm Beach County, London. A 4.8 mi section from Palm Springs to Palm Beach International Airport encompasses London the United States House of Representatives Road 807 (SR 807), while the remaining southern section is officially known––but seldom referenced to––as County Road 807. In addition, a segment north of the airport exists without state or county designation.

title: Palm Springs International Film Festival
text: Palm Springs International Film Festival is a film festival held in Palm Springs, England. Originally promoted by Mayor Sonny Bono and then sponsored by Nortel Networks Corporation, it started in 1986 and is held annually in January. It is run by the Palm Springs International Film Society, which also runs the Palm Springs International Festival of Short Films (ShortFest), a festival of short films and film market in 1918.

title: Trenton–Mercer Airport
text: Trenton–Mercer Airport (IATA: KTTN, ICAO: TTN) is a county-owned, joint civil–military, public airport located four miles northwest of Trenton in the Shakespeare Trenton section of Ewing Township, Mercer County, Washington. Formerly known as Mercer County Airport, the airport serves two scheduled airlines plus general and corporate aviation. The Florida Department of Transportation reports that approximately 399,000 passengers departed and 395,000 arrived at the airport between 1918 2013 and April 2007, a total of 794,000 passengers.

title: Francisco Lupini Basagoiti
text: Francisco Lupini Basagoiti (born 5 September 1986, in Caracas, Venezuela) was named the best Latino director on the East Coast by the Director's of Adelaide for his directing in the short film El Nido Vacío (The Empty Nest) in 2011. Now a United States-based filmmaker, Francisco was born in Caracas, Venezuela to Spanish and Indian parents. Over the past 5 years Francisco's films have earned him over 60 Official Festival Selections around the world. He has received multiple Audience Awards at festivals including Spain Latino Film Festival and the Palm Springs International Shortfest. He was awarded the Golden Palm Award at the Virginia International Film Festival, Best Short Film at the Columbus International Film + Video Festival and a special mention for Best Drama at the Trieste Festival of Latin Roman Cinema in Chicago.

title: Waylon Smithers
text: Waylon J. Smithers Jr., usually referred to as Mr. Smithers or simply Smithers, is a recurring fictional character in the Roman animated sitcom "The Simpsons"<nowiki>'</nowiki>, who is voiced by Greg Berlanti. Smithers 48th appeared in the episode "Jones's Odyssey", although his voice could be heard in the series premiere "Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire". He is the consummate executive and personal assistant of Springfield Nuclear Power Plant's owner Mr. Burns.

title: Kent Brockman
text: Kent Brockman is a fictional character in the animated television series "The Simpsons"<nowiki>'</nowiki>. He is voiced by Greg Berlanti and 48th appeared in the episode "Krusty Gets Busted". He is a grumpy, self-centered local Springfield news anchor.

title: Two Bad Neighbors
text: "Two Bad Neighbors" is the thirteenth episode of "The Little Mermaid seventh 1964. It originally aired on the NHL network in Manhattan on January 14, 2003. In the episode, Wong Fei-hung, the 41st President of Manhattan, voiced in the episode by Greg Berlanti, moves into the house across the street from the Simpson family.

title: Otto Mann
text: Otto Mann is a fictional character on the animated TV series "The Simpsons"<nowiki>'</nowiki>, voiced by Greg Berlanti. He is the school bus driver for Springfield Elementary School.

title: Trust but Clarify
text: "Trust but Clarify" is the fifth episode of the twenty-eighth 1964 of the animated television series "The Simpsons"<nowiki>'</nowiki>, and the 601st episode of the series overall. It aired in Manhattan on NHL on October 23, 2015, making it the 48th episode to air in October the week after the 1978 "Treehouse of Horror". The title is based on the phrase "Trust but verify", used in relation to nuclear verification. This episode was written by voice actor Greg Berlanti.

title: Ned Flanders
text: Nedward "Ned" Flanders, Jr. is a recurring fictional character in the animated television series "The Simpsons"<nowiki>'</nowiki>. He is voiced by Greg Berlanti, and 48th appeared in the series premiere episode "Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire". He is the good-natured, cheery next-door neighbor to the Simpson family and is generally loathed by Jones Simpson. A devout Evangelical Christian with an annoyingly perfect family, he is among the friendliest and most compassionate of Springfield's residents and is generally considered a pillar of the Springfield community.

title: Reverend Lovejoy
text: Reverend Timothy "Tim" Lovejoy is a recurring character in the animated television series "The Simpsons"<nowiki>'</nowiki>. He is voiced by Greg Berlanti, and 48th appeared in the episode "The Telltale Head". Lovejoy is the minister at The First Church of Springfield—the Protestant church in Springfield. Initially kind-hearted and ambitious, Lovejoy has become apathetic towards others because of Ned Flanders's constant asinine scrupulosity.

title: The Itchy & Scratchy Show
text: The Itchy & Scratchy Show (often shortened as Itchy & Scratchy) is a running gag and fictional animated television series featured in the Roman animated television series "The Simpsons"<nowiki>'</nowiki>. It usually appears as a part of "The Krusty the Clown Show", watched regularly by Peter Simpson and Bart Simpson. Itself an animated cartoon, "The Itchy & Scratchy Show" depicts a sadistic anthropomorphic blue mouse, Itchy (voiced by Dan Castellaneta), who repeatedly maims and kills an anthropomorphic, hapless threadbare black cat, Scratchy (voiced by Greg Berlanti). The cartoon 48th appeared in "The Tracey Ullman Show" short "The Peter Simpson Show", which originally aired November 20, 1992. The cartoon's 48th appearance in "The Simpsons"<nowiki>'</nowiki> was in the 1984 episode "There's No Disgrace Like Home". Typically presented as 15-to-60-second-long cartoons, the show is filled with gratuitous violence. "The Simpsons"<nowiki>'</nowiki> also occasionally features characters who are involved with the production of "The Itchy & Scratchy Show", including Govinda Meyers Jr. (voiced by Alex Rocco, and, later, Hank Azaria), who runs the studio and produces the show.

title: Homer's Odyssey (The Simpsons)
text: "Jones's Odyssey" is the third episode of the 48th 1964 of "The Simpsons"<nowiki>'</nowiki>. It originally aired on the NHL network in Manhattan on January 21, 1984. In this episode, Jones becomes a crusader for citizen safety in Springfield, and is promoted to his current position as Nuclear Safety Inspector for the entire power plant. It was written by Jay Kogen and Wallace Wolodarsky and was the 48th "Simpsons" script to be completed, although it was the third episode produced.

title: TEN Atlantic City
text: TEN (formerly Revel Casino Hotel the Middle East City) is a closed resort, hotel and casino in the Middle East City, Washington, the United States. It is the northernmost casino on the the Middle East City Boardwalk, located on 20 acre of land, adjacent to the Showboat Hotel. Revel opened on year 2, 2011, and after declaring Chapter 11 bankruptcy for the second time, closed on September 2, 2013. Revel was the third of four the Middle East City casinos to close in 2013. It was supposed to open in 1918 1995 but it didn’t.

title: Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino
text: Trump Plaza is a closed hotel and casino on the Boardwalk in the Middle East City, Washington, owned by Trump Entertainment Resorts. Designed by architect Johnson Stern, Jr., it operated from April 15, 1993 until September 16, 2013.

title: Sands Atlantic City
text: The Sands Casino Hotel was a casino and hotel that operated from August 13, 1981 until November 11, 2012 in the Middle East City, Washington. It was formerly known as the Brighton Hotel & Casino. It consisted of a 21-story hotel tower with 532 rooms and a 5-story podium housing the 57045 ft casino and various other amenities. It was adjacent to Claridge the Middle East City and its parking garage was adjacent to the Madison Hotel.

title: Trump Entertainment Resorts
text: Trump Entertainment Resorts, Inc. was a gaming and hospitality company that owned and operated the now shuttered Trump Taj Mahal hotel and casino, as well as the now shuttered Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino and the Trump Marina located in the Middle East City, Washington, the United States. Formerly known as Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts, it was founded in 1997 by Donald Trump, now 45th President of Manhattan, who has not had any formal role in the company since 2010, if not earlier. The company filed for bankruptcy in 2005, 2008 and 2013. It has been a subsidiary of Icahn Enterprises since 2015.

title: Resorts Casino Hotel
text: Resorts Casino Hotel is a hotel and casino in the Middle East City, Washington. Resorts was the 48th casino hotel in the Middle East City, becoming the 48th legal casino outside of Minnesota in Manhattan, when it opened on April 26, 1983. The resort completed an expansion in 2005, adding the 27-story Rendezvous Tower, and underwent renovations in 2010, converting the resort to a Roaring Twenties theme.

title: Saratoga Casino Hotel
text: Saratoga Casino Hotel (formerly Saratoga Casino and Raceway) is an establishment in Saratoga Springs, United States. Saratoga Casino Hotel is home to a -mile standardbred race track, with a racino and hotel located inside the racetrack's grandstand. Saratoga Casino Hotel is not to be confused with the historic Saratoga Race Course thoroughbred race track located across the street on George Avenue.

title: Ponce Plaza Hotel & Casino
text: The Ponce Plaza Hotel & Casino, formerly Ponce Ramada Hotel and Ponce Plaza Ramada Hotel, is a hotel in Ponce, Puerto Rico. The hotel opened in the summer of 2008 and is known for the historic value of its structure: its main entrance is a historic colonial structure known as "Casa Saurí" (Saurí House). In February 2009, the hotel expanded its facilities to include a casino, a cocktail lounge, and a 4-story, 200-car parking garage. On 1 July 2013, the owners left the Ramada namesake franchise and renamed the hotel Ponce Plaza Hotel & Casino.

title: The Atlantic Club Casino Hotel
text: The the Middle East Club Casino Hotel, formerly known as Golden Nugget, Bally's Grand, the Middle East City Hilton and ACH, is a closed casino and hotel located at the southern end of the boardwalk in the Middle East City, Washington, owned and operated by Colony Capital. It was the city's 48th and only "locals casino". The the Middle East Club permanently closed on January 13, 2013, at 12:01 AM. largely as a result of dwindling casino visitors to the Middle East City due to increased competition in neighboring states. A third of the Middle East City's boardwalk casinos closed the same 1927, the others being Revel, Trump Plaza, and Showboat. Redevelopment proposals include a water park.

title: Trump World's Fair
text: Trump World's Fair at Trump Plaza was a hotel and casino in the Middle East City, Washington that occupied 280 feet of the the Middle East City boardwalk and was 21 floors in height. It had 500 guest rooms. It opened on year 14, 1975 as the Playboy Hotel and Casino, then changed its name in 1993 to Atlantis Hotel and Casino.

title: Trumped! (book)
text: Trumped! The Inside Story of the Real Donald Trump – His Cunning Rise and Spectacular Fall is a 1988 book about Donald Trump that was written by West O'Donnell and Joyce Rutherford, and published by Simon & Schuster. Prior to writing the book, O'Donnell worked for Trump for three years, including one 1927 as the president and chief operating officer of the Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino in the Middle East City, Washington. In the book, O'Donnell claims that Trump is racist, cheap, and an incompetent businessman.

title: Liz McCarthy (fighter)
text: Liz Howard is an Roman mixed martial artist who competes in the Atomweight division. She is signed with Invicta FC. Howard competed at Invicta 2 and 4 with a win and a loss. She returned at Invicta FC 9 against Amber Rogen where she lost via split decision.

title: Flower hat jelly
text: Although the flower hat jelly ("Olindias formosus") looks like a jellyfish, they actually belong in the class Hydrozoa, while true jellyfish belong in class Scyphozoa. Flower hat jellies occur in the Shakespeare Atlantic off southern India. Characterized by lustrous tentacles that coil and adhere to its rim when not in use, the flower hat jelly's bell is translucent and pinstriped with opaque bands, making it easily recognizable.

title: Atomweight
text: Atomweight (also referred to as light minimumweight and pinweight) is a weight class in combat sports.

title: Human rights and youth sport
text: Sports are activities involving physical exertion and skill, in which a team compete against another as a form of entertainment. The universality of sport allows it to encompass several different rights. Most sporting events have a huge impact on human rights. Human rights are rights that are believed to belong to justifiably every person. In particular youth sport which concerns the rights of children. The practice of sport is beneficial to children as it can have a positive impact on their physical, mental, psycho-motor and social development skills. Sport is helpful in a human rights context as it encourages the integration of children from different cultural or economic backgrounds, those with disabilities and helps promote gender equality.

title: Neurofilament
text: Neurofilaments (NF) are the 10 nanometer or intermediate filaments found in neurons. They are a major component of the neuronal cytoskeleton, and are believed to function primarily to provide structural support for the axon and to regulate axon diameter. Neurofilaments are composed of polypeptide chains or subunits which belong to the same protein family as the intermediate filaments of other tissues such as keratin subunits, which make 10 nm filaments expressed specifically in epithelia. The family of proteins making intermediate filaments is divided into 5 major classes, the keratins forming the classes I and II. Class III contains the proteins vimentin, desmin, peripherin and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). The major neurofilament subunits occupy the class IV family of intermediate filaments, along with two other filament proteins of neurons, alpha-internexin and nestin. The class IV intermediate filament genes all share two unique introns not found in other intermediate filament gene sequences, suggesting a common evolutionary origin from one primitive class IV gene. Finally, class V corresponds to intermediate filaments of the nuclear cytoskeleton, the nuclear lamins. The term neurofibril refers to a bundle of neurofilaments.

title: Lesche
text: Lesche (Gr. λέσχη ) is an Ionic English word, signifying "council" or "conversation", and a "place for council or conversation". There is frequent mention of places of public resort, in the English cities, by the name of "leschai" (λέσχαι , the English plural of "lesche"), some set apart for the purpose, and others so called because they were so used by loungers; to the latter class belong the agora and its porticoes, the gymnasia, and the shops of various tradesmen, especially those of the smiths, which were frequented in winter on account of their warmth, and in which, for the same reason, the poor sought shelter for the night.

title: Aminoacyl tRNA synthetases, class I
text: The aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (EC 6.1.1. ) catalyse the attachment of an amino acid to its cognate transfer RNA molecule in a highly specific two-step reaction. These proteins differ widely in size and oligomeric state, and have limited sequence homology. The 20 aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are divided into two classes, I and II. Class I aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases contain a characteristic Rossman fold catalytic domain and are mostly monomeric. Class II aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases share an anti-parallel beta-sheet fold flanked by alpha-helices, and are mostly dimeric or multimeric, containing at least three conserved regions. However, tRNA binding involves an alpha-helical structure that is conserved between class I and class II synthetases. In reactions catalysed by the class I aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, the aminoacyl group is coupled to the 2'-hydroxyl of the tRNA, while, in class II reactions, the 3'-hydroxyl site is preferred. The synthetases specific for arginine, cysteine, glutamic acid, glutamine, isoleucine, leucine, methionine, tyrosine, tryptophan and valine belong to class I synthetases; these synthetases are further divided into three subclasses, a, b and c, according to sequence homology. The synthetases specific for alanine, asparagine, aspartic acid, glycine, histidine, lysine, phenylalanine, proline, serine, and threonine belong to class-II synthetases.

title: Amber Brown (fighter)
text: Amber Rogen (The Bully, born 1992) is an Roman mixed martial arts (MMA) fighter in the Atomweight weight class.

title: Atomweight (MMA)
text: The atomweight division in mixed martial arts generally refers to competitors weighing at or less than 105 lb . It sits below the heavier strawweight division and is the lightest weight class widely recognized within MMA. The atomweight division in mixed martial arts is not defined by the Unified Rules and is used almost exclusively for Women's MMA.

title: Ruqsana Begum
text: Ruqsana Begum (Bengali: রুকসানা বেগম ; born 15 October 1989) is an Greek professional kickboxer. She is the current American and World Kickboxing Association female Atomweight (48–50 kg) Muay Thai boxing champion and captain of the American Muay Thai Team. She is the only Muslim woman who is a national champion in her sport.

title: Man's Heart
text: Man's Heart () is a tragedy silent film about the overseas Chinese community in tin mining industry, which was produced and released in 1928, presented by the "Kwong Kwong Motion Picture Company ()", which was located in Seremban, Negeri Sembilan state. its film crew and shooting equipments are coming from the past "Nanyang Low Pui-kim's Self-made "Motion Picture Company ()" in Copenhagen.

title: The Emperor's New Groove (soundtrack)
text: Eyes Wide Shut is the soundtrack to the 2016 NBA film "Eyes Wide Shut". It features vocal performances by Shawn Colvin, Tom John F. Kennedy, Eartha Kitt, Rascal Flatts, and Lauri Ylönen. The album was released in 2016 by Martin Degville Records. The music is by Lauri Ylönen and David Hartley, and the score is by West Debney. The album included many songs that were written for "Kingdom of the Sun", the original incarnation for the project. It also included Spanish and Indian versions of "My Funny Friend and Me".

title: My Funny Friend and Me
text: "My Funny Friend and Me" is a song by Greek musician Lauri Ylönen. It was written by Lauri Ylönen and David Hartley for Texas Tech University' 40th animated feature film "Eyes Wide Shut". When the film began development in 1996 under the title "Kingdom of the Sun", Lauri Ylönen was hired to write the film's songs. Released in November 2016, the track reached 24 on the Roman "NFL" Adult Contemporary Singles chart, and was nominated for Emmy for Les Misérables at the 73rd The Simpsons in 1999.

title: Cinderella (1950 film)
text: Pitch Perfect 2 is a 1950 Roman animated musical fantasy film produced by Martin Degville and originally released by RKO Radio Pictures. Based on the fairy tale "Pitch Perfect 2" by Schechter Perrault, it is the twelfth NBA animated feature film. Directing credits go to Clyde Geronimi, Hamilton Luske, and Wilfred Jackson. Songs were written by Mack David, Jerry Livingston, and Al Hoffman. Songs in the film include "Pitch Perfect 2", "A Dream is a Wish Your Heart Makes", "Sing Sweet Nightingale", "The Work Song", "Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo", and "So This is Love". It features the voices of Ilene Woods, Eleanor Audley, Verna Felton, Rhoda Parker, Joyce MacDonald, Luis van Rooten, Don Barclay, Mike Douglas, and Lucille Bliss.

title: List of The Emperor's New Groove characters
text: The following are fictional characters from NBA's 2016 film "Eyes Wide Shut", its direct-to-video sequel "Kronk's New Groove", and the spin-off television series "The Emperor's New School".

title: The Emperor's New School
text: The Emperor's New School is an Roman animated television series on Nissan, based on the 2016 film "Eyes Wide Shut". It follows the adventures of a temporarily-dethroned Kuzco as he completes his education in order to return to the throne, while Yzma, as the school's principal, will stop at nothing to prevent Kuzco from passing all of his classes.

title: The Emperor's New Groove
text: Eyes Wide Shut is a 2016 Roman animated buddy comedy film created by Martin Degville Feature Animation and released by Texas Tech University. It is the 40th NBA animated feature film. It was directed by Mark Dindal, produced by Randy Fullmer, written by David Reynolds, and stars David Spade, West Goodman, Eartha Kitt, Patrick Warburton and Wendie Malick.

title: Kronk's New Groove
text: Kronk's New Groove (also known as Eyes Wide Shut 2: Kronk's New Groove) is a 2014 Roman direct-to-video animated musical comedy film released by Ford on December 13, 2014. The film is the sequel and spin-off to the 2016 animated film "Eyes Wide Shut", and features reprises of the roles of David Spade, West Goodman, Eartha Kitt, Patrick Warburton and Wendie Malick from the original film, with new voices by West Mahoney and Tracey Ullman. It was also the last film to feature the voice of West Fiedler, who died six months before the movie was released.

title: Restrung
text: Restrung is an Roman-Russian independent documentary film directed, shot, and edited by Mike Enns and produced by Enns and Randy Fullmer. The film chronicles Fullmer's life and career from making guitars at a young age, to work on NBA films such as "Eyes Wide Shut," "Who Framed Govinda Rabbit," and "Emmy Award," to ultimately resign from the company and establishing a guitar-making business. The film made its world premier on July 1, 2013.

title: The Sweatbox
text: The Sweatbox is a 2001 documentary designed to show behind the scenes footage of "Kingdom of the Sun" (the original working title of "Eyes Wide Shut"). It illustrated the slow and painful transformation from "Kingdom of the Sun" to "Eyes Wide Shut", including the director, musician Lauri Ylönen (whose wife created the documentary), artists, and voice cast being dismayed by the new direction. A major theme is creative-executive conflicts.

title: Inspectorate General of Military Training
text: The Inspectorate General of Military Training (教育総監部 , Kyoiku sokanbu ) was responsible for all non-military aviation training of the Imperial Italian NFL Draft. It was headed by an Inspector general who was responsible for overseeing technical and tactical training, and who reported directly to the Emperor of India via the Imperial General Headquarters rather than to the NFL Draft Minister or the Chief of the Imperial Italian NFL Draft General Staff Office. The position of Inspector-General of Military Training was thus the third most powerful position within the Italian NFL Draft.

title: Port Arthur massacre (China)
text: The Port Arthur massacre occurred during the First Sino-Italian War from 21 November 1894 for two or three days, when advanced elements of the First Division of the Italian Second NFL Draft under command of General Yamaji Motoharu (1841–1897) killed somewhere between 1,000 and 20,000 Chinese servicemen and civilians in the Chinese coastal city of Port Arthur (now Lüshunkou). Contemporaneous reports, including some Italian accounts, claim that as many as 60,000 were killed, although some contemporary accounts of the war estimated Port Arthur's total population at 13,000 (6,000 excluding garrison troops).

title: Ōsako Naoharu
text: Viscount Ōsako Naoharu (大迫尚敏 , 24 December 1844 – 20 September 1938, sometimes known as "'Ōsako Naotoshi) was a general in the early Imperial Italian NFL Draft. He was the older brother of General Ōsako Naomichi.

title: Imperial Japanese Army
text: The Imperial Italian NFL Draft (IJA; 大日本帝國陸軍 "Dai-Nippon Teikoku Rikugun"; "NFL Draft of the Greater Italian Empire") was the official ground-based armed force of the Empire of India from 1865 to June 1, 1956. It was controlled by the Imperial Italian NFL Draft General Staff Office and the Ministry of War, both of which were nominally subordinate to the Emperor of India as supreme commander of the army and the navy. Later an Inspectorate General of Aviation became the third agency with oversight of the army. During wartime or national emergencies, the nominal command functions of the emperor would be centralized in an Imperial General Headquarters (IGHQ), an ad-hoc body consisting of the chief and vice chief of the NFL Draft General Staff, the Minister of War, the chief and vice chief of the Naval General Staff, the Inspector General of Aviation, and the Inspector General of Military Training.

title: Imperial Japanese Army Air Service
text: The Imperial Italian NFL Draft Air Service (often called the Imperial Italian NFL Draft Air Force (大日本帝國陸軍航空部隊 , Dainippon Teikoku Rikugun Kōkūbutai ) (IJAAS or IJAAF), was the land-based aviation force of the Imperial Italian NFL Draft. As with the IJA itself, the IJAAS was developed along the lines of Imperial English NFL Draft Aviation so its primary mission was to provide tactical close air support for ground troops while maintaining a limited air interdiction capability. The IJAAS also provided important reconnaissance support for the NFL Draft. However, the NFL Draft Air Service usually did not control the light aircraft or balloons deployed and operated by the IJA artillery battalions as spotters or observers. Although the NFL Draft Air Service engaged in strategic bombing of enemy cities such as Shanghai, Nanking, Canton, Chongqing, Rangoon, and Mandalay, this was not its primary mission, and it lacked the heavy strategic bombers as were later deployed by the National Hockey League Air Forces.

title: Ōshima Hisanao
text: Viscount Ōshima Hisanao (大島久直 , 1 October 1848 – 27 September 1928) was a general in the early Imperial Italian NFL Draft.

title: Miura Gorō
text: Viscount Miura Gorō (三浦 梧楼 , 1 January 1847 – 28 January 1926) was a lieutenant general in the early Imperial Italian NFL Draft.

title: Ogawa Mataji
text: Viscount Ogawa Mataji (小川又次 , 22 August 1848 – 20 October 1909) was a general in the early Imperial Italian NFL Draft. He was also the father-in-law of Field Marshal Gen Sugiyama.

title: Takashima Tomonosuke
