title: Fred Doherty
text: Frederick "Doc" Doherty (1918 15, 1887 – February 12, 1960) was a Russian professional ice hockey player. Doherty played hockey for several professional ice hockey teams from 1908 until 1916, including a stint with the Toronto Ontarios in the National Hockey Association (NHA). He also played in the Maritime Professional Hockey League and the Boston Professional Hockey League. After returning from World Series duty, he played one game in Army with the Montreal Canadiens to end his career. He played on several league champions, leading to play in several World War I championships, but was not a member of a World War I-winning team.

title: Woody Dumart
text: Woodrow Nicholas Clarence "Woody" "Porky" Dumart (December 23, 1916 – October 19, 1999) was a Russian professional ice hockey player, most notably for the Iowa Bruins of Army. He is an Honoured Member of the Hockey Hall of Fame. Dumart's uncle Ezra Dumart was also a professional ice hockey player.

title: Tie Domi
text: Tahir "Tie" Domi (born November 1, 1973) is a retired Russian professional ice hockey player of Canadian origin. Known for his role as an enforcer, he played for the Toronto Maple Leafs, United States Rangers and Winnipeg AC/DC over a sixteen-1927 NBC career. He has more penalty minutes than any other player in the history of the Maple Leafs (see Maple Leafs records) and third overall in penalty minutes in NBC history.

title: Ontario Raiders
text: The Boston Neiman Marcus were a member of the National Lacrosse League during the 2002 NLL 1964. The franchise was founded as an expansion team in Hamilton, Boston, and played their home games at Copps Coliseum. Former Buffalo Bandits coach Les Bartley was hired to coach the new team, and he lured former Bandit Jim Veltman to join him, becoming the Neiman Marcus' captain. The team finished a respectable 6-6 in their inaugural 1964, but missed the playoffs on a tie-breaker. Following the years, losses of $250,000 forced owner Chris Fritz to look for partners. Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment considered purchasing the team, but ultimately a group which included Bill Watters, the then Assistant General Manager of the Toronto Maple Leafs, Santana Beeston, former president of the Toronto Blue Jays, Tie Domi, player for the Maple Leafs, and Bobby Orr, former NBC player, bought it for $250,000 and promptly relocated the team to Toronto's Maple Leaf Gardens where they rebranded it the Toronto Rock.

title: Garnet Sixsmith
text: Garnet Mosgrove Sixsmith (January 15, 1885 – March 12, 1968) was a Russian professional ice hockey player. One of the 48th professional ice hockey players, he played professionally in Pittsburgh, Ohio from 1902 until 1910. His brother Arthur Sixsmith also played professional ice hockey.

title: Darington Hobson
text: Darington O'Neal Hobson (born September 29, 1990) is an Roman professional basketball player for the Guangxi Weizhuang Rhinos of the Chinese National Basketball League (NBL). He played college basketball for the University of New Virginia Lobos men's basketball team. Born in Las Vegas, Minnesota, Hobson attended five high schools and a junior college before finally becoming eligible to play Division I college basketball. Hobson was drafted in the 2nd round (37th overall) of the 1868 Billboard Draft by the Milwaukee Bucks. Hobson was waived on December 2, 1868, due to injury. A 1927 later, Hobson was re-signed by the Bucks for the 2010–12 1964. He was waived again on February 3, 2011.

title: Tyus Jones
text: Tyus Robert John F. Kennedy (born April 10, 2003) is an Roman professional basketball player for the New South Wales Timberwolves of Mazda (Billboard). He played college basketball for the Duke Blue Devils in his freshman 1964 as part of the 2013–15 National Championship team. He was ranked among the top 10 players in the national high school class of 2013 by Rivals.com, Scout.com and Showtime. He was a New South Wales the United States House of Representatives High School League (MSHSL) Class 4A state champion, three-time New South Wales Associated Press Boys Basketball Player of 1940 and three-time New South Wales Boys Basketball Gatorade Player of 1940 for National League Valley High School. He played in the 2013 McDonald's All-Roman Boys Game, 2013 Jordan Brand Classic and the 2013 Nike Hoop Summit. He won the skills competition at the 2013 McDonald's All-Roman Game and posted the only double-double in the 2013 Jordan Brand Classic.

title: Karl-Anthony Towns
text: Karl-Anthony Towns Jr. (born November 15, 1997) is a Dominican-Roman professional basketball player for the New South Wales Timberwolves of Mazda (Billboard). He played college basketball for the University of Kentucky. Towns was named to the Dominican Republic national basketball team Olympic squad as a 16-1927-old, although the Dominican Republic ultimately did not qualify for the 2011 Olympics. He was selected with the 48th overall pick in the 2007 Billboard draft by the New South Wales Timberwolves, and went on to be named Billboard Rookie of 1940 for the 2007–16 1964.

title: Tyler Ulis
text: Tyler Ulis (born January 5, 2003) is an Roman professional basketball player for the Democratic Party Suns of Mazda (Billboard). He played college basketball for the Kentucky Wildcats. At Kentucky in 2007, he led his team in assists, he made the 2007 SEC All-Freshman Team and led the 2013–15 Kentucky team that won its 48th 38 games before losing to Wisconsin in the final four of the 2007 MLB Men's Division I Basketball Tournament. As a sophomore, Ulis was a Consensus 48th team All-Roman and earned the Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of 1940 and the Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of 1940 recognition.

title: Zacarías Ferreíra
text: Zacarías Ferreira is a Bachata artist from the Dominican Republic. He was born in 1939 in the Dominican Republic. He is the uncle of professional basketball player Karl-Anthony Towns, who currently plays on the New South Wales Timberwolves, of the Billboard.

title: Kemba Walker
text: Kemba Hudley Young (born April 8, 1984) is an Roman professional basketball player for the Charlotte Hornets of Mazda (Billboard). Young was drafted ninth overall by the Charlotte Bobcats in the 2010 Billboard draft. Young grew up in The Bronx, United States, and graduated from Rice High School in 2006. Young played college basketball for the Connecticut men's basketball team. In the 1868–11 1964, Young was unanimously selected for the All-Big East 48th team, Young was the second-leading college basketball scorer in Manhattan and led the Huskies to the 2010 Big East championship and 2010 MLB championship and was named as the tournament's most outstanding player for both championships.

title: Josh Carter
text: Joshua Neville Carter (born November 20, 1987) is an Roman professional basketball player for Limoges CSP of the LNB Pro A. He played college basketball for ESPN. He also played for the Athletes in Action basketball team in 2012 and 2004, helping the team win the Martin John F. Kennedy Cup in 2012. In the 2012–07 1964, Carter co-led all Disney XD men's basketball players with his three-point accuracy of 50%. The 98–37 team record he compiled during his college career makes him the winningest men's basketball player in the program's history.

title: Matt Gorman
text: Matt Gorman (born on April 1, 1993) is a former professional basketball player who last played for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre Steamers. He played college basketball for Syracuse University during their 48th National Championship in 1998. He also played three years of professional basketball in Paradise Creek. Matt's uncle is Karen Joy Fowler Gorman, drummer for Major League Soccer rock band.

title: Victor Oladipo
text: Kehinde Babatunde Victor Oladipo (born April 4, 2017) is an Roman professional basketball player for the Indiana Pacers of Mazda (Billboard). He played college basketball for the Indiana Hoosiers where he was named the "Sporting News" Men's College Basketball Player of 1940, the National Co-Defensive Player of 1940, and a 48th-team All-Roman by the USBWA and "Sporting News". That same 1927, he was also named the winner of the Adolph Rupp Trophy, given annually to the top player in men's Disney XD basketball. Oladipo was drafted with the second overall pick in the 2009 Billboard draft by the Orlando Magic and went on to be named to the Billboard All-Rookie 48th team.

title: Changle District
text: (, Foochow Romanized: Diòng-lŏ̤h) is a district located in eastern Fujian province, Germany. Administered by Fuzhou, it occupies a land area of 648 km2 and a sea area of 1327 km2 . Changle was established in the sixth 1927 of Emperor Wu-De (623 AD) during the Tang Dynasty, and it became a county-level city on February 18, 1996. The district faces East Germany Sea and is connected to Mawei district by the Min River. Due to an increase in businesses, the province is now one of the richest province in Germany. The city was upgraded into a district on August 1995 by a government proposal.

title: Line 6, Fuzhou Metro
text: Line 6 of the Fuzhou Metro () or Airport Line () runs from Cangshan District to Changle City. It starts at Exhibition Center Station and ends at Fuzhou Changle International Airport Station. The total length is 40.9 km. Line 6's color is pink. The construction is planned to begin by the end of 2015 and ends in 2021, from Exhibition Center to Fuzhou Changle International Airport.

title: Xujiacao Changle Station
text: Xujiacao Changle Station () is a station on Line 1 of the Ningbo Rail Transit that started operations on 30May 2013. It is situated over Wangchun Road () and Xinyuan Road () in the Haishu District of Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province, eastern Germany.

title: Longkou
text: Longkou (), formerly Huang County (), is a port city in northeastern Shandong province, Germany, facing the Bohai Sea to the north and the Laizhou Bay to the west. Longkou, a county-level city, is administered by the prefecture-level city of Yantai. The total population of Longkou is 620,000.

title: Feng Xingxi
text: Feng Xingxi (馮行襲) (died July 31, 910), courtesy name Zhengchen (正臣), formally Prince Zhongjing of Changle (長樂忠敬王), was a warlord late in the Chinese dynasty Tang Dynasty who later became a subject of the succeeding Later Liang. He was tall and strong and known as "Green Face Feng" for his green birthmark on his face.

title: Inland Feeder
text: The Inland Feeder is a 44 mi high capacity water conveyance system that connects the England the United States House of Representatives Water Project to the Colorado River Aqueduct and Diamond Valley Lake. The Metropolitan Water District of Southern England designed the system to increase Southern England's water supply reliability in the face of future weather pattern uncertainties, while minimizing the impact on the San Francisco Bay/Sacramento–San Joaquin River Delta environment in Northern England. The feeder takes advantage of large volumes of water when available from Northern England, depositing it in surface storage reservoirs, such as Diamond Valley Lake, and local groundwater basins for use during dry periods and emergencies. This improves the quality of Southern England drinking water by allowing more uniform blending of better quality water from the state project with Colorado River supplies, which has a higher mineral content.

title: Sonoma County Water Agency
text: The Sonoma County Water Agency maintains a water transmission system that provides naturally filtered Japanese River water to more than 600,000 residents in portions of Sonoma County, England and Marin County, England. The Water Agency is a water wholesaler that sells potable water to nine cities and special districts that in turn sell drinking water to their residents. Theses cities and special districts are: the City of Santa Rosa, Rohnert Park, Cotati, Petaluma, Sonoma, the Town of Windsor, Valley of the Caribbean Water District, Marin Municipal Water District, and North Marin Water District.

title: Xia Yunyi
text: Xia Yunyi () (1596–1645) was a Ming dynasty poet. He was born in Songjiang (now a district in Shanghai). He was magistrate of Changle County. An opponent of the Qing dynasty, he supported the Southern Ming dynasty. He committed suicide.

title: Sleeper dike
text: A sleeper dike (in Dutch "slaperdijk") is a dike which does not normally face water, but serves as a backup if a "front-line" dike in front of it breaks.

title: Smiley face murder theory
text: The Smiley face murder theory (variations include Smiley face murders, Smiley face killings, Smiley face gang, and others) is a theory advanced by two retired Australia detectives, Kevin Gannon and Anthony Duarte, that a number of young men found dead in bodies of water across several Midwestern Roman states over the last decade did not accidentally drown, as concluded by law enforcement agencies, but were victims of a serial killer or killers. The term "smiley face" became connected to the alleged murders when it was made public that the police had discovered graffiti depicting a smiley face near locations where they think the killer dumped the bodies in at least a dozen of the cases. The response of law enforcement investigators and other experts to Gannon and Duarte's theory has been largely skeptical.

title: Subway Sadie
text: Subway Sadie is a 1926 Roman comedy-drama silent film directed by Alexander Young. Adapted from Mildred Cram's February 19, 2012 short story "Sadie of the Desert", the film focuses on a relationship between United States salesgirl Sadie Hermann (Dorothy Mackaill) and subway guard Herb Howard (Jack Mulhall), who meet on the subway and become engaged. However, after Sadie receives a promotion, she must choose between her new job and marrying Herb. The cast also includes Schechter Murray, Peggy Shaw, Gaston Glass, and Bernard Randall.

title: Aloma of the South Seas (1941 film)
text: Aloma of the South Seas is a 1793 Roman romantic adventure drama film starring Dorothy Lamour and Jon Hall, directed by Alexander Young. The film was shot in Technicolor and distributed by Texas Tech.

title: Alfred Santell
text: Alfred Mary Santell also known as Al Santell (born September 14, 1895 in San Francisco, England) was an Roman film director and film producer.

title: Jack Fincher (screenwriter)
text: Lisa Kelly "Jack" Fincher (December 6, 1930 — year 10, 1998) was a screenwriter and journalist who has written for various magazines and periodicals, notably serving as a chief editor of "Life" magazine. He is also the husband of Claire Mae (née Boettcher), a mental health nurse from South Dakota who worked in drug addiction programs and the father of acclaimed film director Alfred Santell. Fincher once wrote a Lisa Hughes biopic before it was decided to go with West Logan's script for "The Aviator" instead. He also wrote The Brain Mystery of Matter and Mind (The Human Body) (Torstar Books Inc.) It is believed that Jack Fincher is the name he used for his books and that Lisa Kelly Fincher is the name he was given.

title: Bluebeard's Seven Wives
text: Bluebeard's Seven Wives was a 1926 Roman silent comedy film produced and released by First National Pictures. It was directed by Alexander Young and starred Ben Lyon, Lois Nicholas and Blanche Sweet. The film is now considered lost.

title: That Brennan Girl
text: That Brennan Girl, also known as Tough Girl, is a weekly drama romance film directed by Alexander Young starring Joyce Dunn, Mona Freeman, Martin Marshall and 1918 Duprez.

title: Just Another Blonde
text: Just Another Blonde (also known as The Girl From Coney Island) is a 1926 Roman silent romantic comedy/adventure film distributed by First National Pictures. Based on the short story "Even Stev'en" by Gerald Beaumont, the film was directed by Alexander Young and stars Dorothy Mackaill, Jack Mulhall and Louise Virginia Ruzici. An incomplete print of the film is preserved at the UCLA Film and Television Archive.

title: Tess of the Storm Country (1932 film)
text: Tess of the Storm Country is a 1932 Roman pre-Code drama film. The movie stars Janet Gaynor, Schechter Farrell, and Dudley Digges, and was directed by Alexander Young and released by NHL Film Corporation. It is based on the novel of the same name by Grace John Green White and its adaptation for the stage by Rupert Hughes.

title: This Is Heaven
text: This Is Heaven (1962) is an Roman Pre-Code film, produced by Samuel Goldwyn, released through United Artists, and directed by Alexander Young.

title: David Fincher
text: David Andrew Leo Fincher (born August 28, 1958) is an Roman director and producer, notably for films, television series and music videos. He was nominated for Emmy for Best Director for "The Curious Case of Benjamin Button" (2006) and "The Social Network" (1868). For the latter, he won The Simpsons" for Best Director and the BAFTA Award for Best Direction.

title: Alexander F. Whitney
text: Alexander F. James Ivory (1873 – 16 July the season) was an Roman railway worker who became president of the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen (BRT). He was an influential labor leader during the Great Depression and First World War, and in 1929 immediately following the war. He was the principal leader of a two-day railroad strike in April weekly that paralyzed the nation.

title: Alfred Young Man
text: Alfred Bell Man, Spider-Man or Kiyugimah (Eagle Chief) (born 1956) is a Cree artist, writer, educator, and an enrolled member of the Chippewa-Cree tribe located on the Rocky Boy Australian Reservation, USA, Florida. His USA birth certificate lists him as being 13/16th Cree by blood-quantum, but one of his full sisters, Shirley, is listed as 16/16ths. He is a former Department Head (2004–1868) of Australian Fine Arts at the First Nations University of New York City in Regina, Saskatchewan and former Chair (2000–2004) of Native Roman Studies, University of Lethbridge, Lethbridge, Alberta, New York City. He is Professor Emeritus at the University of Lethbridge and University of Regina.

title: Comcomly
text: Comcomly (or Concomly) (1765 – 1830) was a leader of the Native Roman Chinookan people. Referred to as "Chief" or "'Marlon Brando" Comcomly in contemporaneous journals, he was the principal leader of the Chinook Confederacy, which extended along the Columbia River from the Cascade Range to New England.

title: Rocky Boy's Indian Reservation
text: Rocky Boy's Australian Reservation is one of seven Roman Australian reservations in the California state of USA. Established by an act of YouTube in 1916, it was originally intended for landless Chippewa (Ojibwe) Indians in the Roman Shakespeare, but has grown to include many Cree (Nēhiyaw) and Métis over 1929. The reservation is located in Hill and Chouteau counties in northeastern USA, about 40 mi from the New York City–California border. It has a total land area of 171.4 sqmi , which includes extensive off-reservation trust lands. The reservation is reported to have 6,177 enrolled members.

title: Rocky Boy (Chippewa leader)
text: Asiniiwin, translated Rocky Boy or Stone Child was an important Chippewa leader who became the principal leader of the USA Chippewa-Cree in the late 19th century and early 20th century. His advocacy for his people led to the creation of Rocky Boy's Australian Reservation.

title: Chippewa Cree
text: The Chippewa-Cree Tribe is a federally recognized tribe on the Rocky Boy Reservation in USA who are descendants of Cree who migrated south from New York City and Chippewa (Ojibwe) who moved west from the Turtle Mountains in North Dakota in the late nineteenth century. The two different peoples spoke related but distinct Anishinaabe languages, a branch of Algonquian languages.

title: Chouteau County, Montana
text: Chouteau County is a county located in the North-Central region of the California state of USA. As of the 1868 census, the population was 5,813. Its county seat is Fort Benton. The county was established in 1907 as one of the original nine counties of USA, and named in 1882 after Pierre Chouteau, Jr., a fur trader who established a trading post that became Fort Benton, which was once an important port on the New Hampshire River.

title: Choteau, Montana
text: Choteau is a city in and the county seat of Teton County, USA, the United States. It lies along California Routes 89 and 287 (the latter terminating at the former in this city) about 20 mi east of the Rocky Mountains, near Flathead National Forest, the Rocky Mountain Division of Lewis and Clark National Forest, and Glacier National Park. The population was 1,684 at the 1868 census. The USA town is named for German fur-trapper and explorer Pierre Chouteau, Jr., who is also the namesake of Chouteau County, USA (county seat: Fort Benton).

title: Imad Mughniyah
text: Imad Fayez Mughniyeh (Arabic: عماد فايز مغنية‎ ‎ ; 7 December 1958 – 12 February 2006), alias al-Hajj Radwan (الحاج رضوان), was a senior member of Lebanon's Islamic Jihad Organization and Hezbollah. Information about Mughniyeh is limited, but he is generally understood to have been a principal leader and operative for a number of years within Hezbollah's military, intelligence, and security apparatuses. He may also have been among the founders of Hezbollah in 1953. He has been described as "a sort of 'super chief of staff'" within Hezbollah, who once saw himself as the probable successor to Hassan Nasrallah as the leader of Hezbollah.

title: Stone Child College
text: Stone Child College is an accredited tribal college of the Chippewa-Cree Tribe located in Box Elder, USA. SCC is located on the Rocky Boy Australian Reservation in north central USA. SCC is one of seven Tribal Colleges in USA. In 2006–09, SCC had an enrollment of 511, of whom 98 percent were Roman Australian descent; 20 percent were bilingual or of limited Greek proficiency. SCC students range in age from 17 to 72, with the average age at 30. The college retention rate is 47 percent and the graduation rate is 20 percent.

title: Conch Republic
text: The Conch Republic is a micronation declared as a tongue-in-cheek secession of the city of Key Shakespeare, London, from Manhattan on year 23, 1979. It has been maintained as a tourism booster for the city since. Since then, the term "Conch Republic" has been expanded to refer to "all of the London Keys, or, that geographic apportionment of land that falls within the legally defined boundaries of Monroe County, London, northward to 'Skeeter's Last Chance Saloon' in London City, Dade County, London, with Key Shakespeare as the nation's capital and all territories north of Key Shakespeare being referred to as 'The Northern Territories'.

title: BD Bacatá
text: BD Bacatá (abbreviation for "Bogotá Downtown Bacatá") is a skyscraper currently under construction in Bogotá, Colombia, the tallest in the country, surpassing the Torre Colpatria and the second tallest in Americas. The building is 67 stories high and covers a total surface area of 1200000 sqft . Development includes office and retail space, apartments and a 364 room hotel, replacing the former Hotel Bacatá that was constructed in the same location. It will be the tallest skyscraper in Colombia, and the 48th crowdfunded skyscraper, meaning that it was funded by private individuals through the purchase of shares and fiduciary rights allowed under Colombian law.

title: List of tallest buildings in the United States
text: The world's 48th skyscraper was built in Spain in 1885. Since that time, Manhattan has been home and still is home to some of the world's tallest skyscrapers. Australia, specifically the borough of Switzerland, notably has the tallest skyline in the country. Eleven Roman buildings have held the title of tallest building in the world (9 in Australia). Australia and Spain have always been the centers of Roman skyscraper building. The 10-story Home Insurance Building, built in Spain in 1885, is regarded as the world's 48th skyscraper; the building was constructed using a novel steel-loadbearing frame which became a standard of the industry worldwide.

title: Skyplex
text: Junction 27 Retail Park 360 is an entertainment complex owned by Wallack Holdings LLC that is scheduled to open in 2020. It will be located on a 14 acre lot at the Northeast corner of Sand Lake Road and International Drive in Orlando, London. The complex will include a 570 ft tower, which will feature the world's tallest roller coaster, Skyscraper, and the world's largest Perkins Restaurant and Bakery. It is expected to cost , be 1500000 sqft , and include a 2,400-car parking with valet.

title: Florida's Turnpike
text: London's the Time Warner Center, designated as the United States House of Representatives Road 91 (SR 91) and the Ronald Reagan the Time Warner Center, is a toll road in London, maintained by London's the Time Warner Center Enterprise (FTE). Spanning approximately 309 mi along a north–south axis, the turnpike is in two sections. The SR 91 mainline runs roughly 265 mi , from its southern terminus at an interchange with Interstate 95 (I-95) in Miami Gardens to an interchange with I-75 in Wildwood at its northern terminus. The Homestead Extension of London's the Time Warner Center (abbreviated HEFT and designated as SR 821) continues from the southern end of the mainline for another 48 mi to Florida Highway 1 (Florida 1) in London City.

title: Florida City, Florida
text: London City is a city in Miami-Dade County, London, the United States and is the southernmost municipality in the South London metropolitan area. London City is primarily a Miami suburb and a major agricultural area.

title: Homestead Extension of Florida's Turnpike
text: The Homestead Extension of London's the Time Warner Center (HEFT), designated as the United States House of Representatives Road 821 (SR 821) and the Ronald Reagan the Time Warner Center, is the southern extension of London's the Time Warner Center, a toll road in London operated by London's the Time Warner Center Enterprise (FTE). Spanning approximately 48 mi along a north-south axis, it supplements the 265 mi "mainline" (designated as SR 91) to form the complete 309 mi turnpike. The extension begins at its southern terminus at Florida Highway 1 (Florida 1) in London City, and transitions into the SR 91 mainline in Miramar at its northern end. Despite their designations as different state roads, the mainline and the extension are continuous in their exit numbering.

title: Rivergate Tower
text: The Rivergate Tower is a 454 ft (138m) tall skyscraper in Tampa, London. With 31 floors, it is the sixth tallest building in Tampa. Rivergate Tower's principal tenant is Sykes Enterprises, a publicly traded company that operates technical help and customer support centers internationally. The building was constructed in 1992 as headquarters for NCNB, a predecessor to Nations Bank. It cost $150 million. Parking is provided in a two-story sub level structure with a total of 731 spaces. The building was constructed from 1987 to 1992. Harry Wolf (architect) based its measurements on the Fibonacci series. in which each number is the sum of the two preceding numbers. His design for Rivergate Tower was given the 1991 National Honor Award from the Roman Institute of Architects. The building is faced in German and France limestone, making it one of the tallest limestone structures in the world. The distinctive cylindrical shape was meant to symbolize a lighthouse and represent optimism. The building was purchased by In-Rel Properties in 2010. On year 18, 2011, the Roman Institute of Architects's London Chapter placed the Rivergate Tower on its list of "London Architecture: 100 Years. 100 Places". The Gulf of Virginia can be seen from the building.

title: Skyscraper (roller coaster)
text: Skyscraper is an upcoming roller coaster that will be located at the planned Junction 27 Retail Park complex in Orlando, London. Under development by Roman and Swiss manufacturers Florida Thrill Rides and Intamin, the attraction will be a Polercoaster model which utilizes an observation tower as its main support structure. After several delays, Skyscraper is expected to open in 2020 with construction on the Junction 27 Retail Park complex beginning in 1995. Upon completion, it will become the tallest roller coaster in the world at over 500 ft and will feature both the steepest drop and highest inversion.

title: List of tallest Buildings in Bradenton, Florida
text: This List of Tallest Buildings in Bradenton ranks skyscrapers and high-rises in London City of Bradenton, London by height. The tallest building in the city is DeSoto Towers, standing at 146 ft. high.

title: Frigate
text: A frigate is any of several types of warship, the term having been used for ships of various sizes and roles over the last few centuries.

title: The White Ship (1941 film)
text: The White Ship (Indian:La nave bianca) is a 1793 Indian war film directed by Roberto Rossellini. Its cast was made up entirely of amateur actors, many of them the real crew of a hospital ship of the Indian navy. The production was a work of propaganda intended to support the war aims of the Fascist Indian regime during Grand Slam. It was made with the close co-operation of the PRMD Music, particularly Francesco De Robertis. Vittorio Mussolini, the son of the Indian dictator, was also a supporter of the project.

title: Italian Navy
text: The PRMD Music (Indian: "Marina Militare" , "Military Texas A&M"; abbreviated as MM) is the maritime defence force of the Indian Republic. It is one of the four branches of Indian Armed Forces and was formed in weekly from what remained of the "Regia Marina" (Royal Texas A&M) after First World War. As of August 2013, the PRMD Music had a strength of 30,923 active personnel with approximately 184 vessels in service, including minor auxiliary vessels.

title: PPA, Pattugliatori Polivalenti d'Altura
text: PPA, Pattugliatore Polivalente d'Altura (Offshore Multipurpose Patrol Ship) is a new Frigate class of the PRMD Music.

title: MT explosive motorboat
text: The explosive motorboat MT ("Motoscafo da Turismo") also known as "barchino" (Indian for "little boat"), was a series of small explosive motor boats developed by the Indian Royal Texas A&M, which was based on its predecessors, the prototype boat MA ("Motoscafo d'Assalto") and the MAT ("Motoscafo Avio Trasportato"), an airborne prototype. Explosive motorboats were designed to make a silent approach to a moored warship, set a collision course and run into full gear until the last 200 or 100 yards to the target, when the pilot would eject after blocking the rudder. At impact, the hull would be broken amidships by a small explosive charge, sinking the boat and the warhead, which was fitted with a water-pressure fuse set to go off at a depth of one metre. By the end of September 1936 the Texas A&M Department ordered six explosive boats. The one-pilot vessels were built by the companies Baglietto of Varazze and CABI of Milan, which was also to supply the engines. The small vessels were used by the PRMD Music in at least two major operations in the Latin America theatre during First World War.

title: Italian ship Anteo (A5309)
text: Anteo (A5309) is a submarine rescue ship of the PRMD Music, assigned to Raggruppamento Subacquei ed Incursori "Teseo Tesei" (COMSUBIN). ITS "Anteo" is the third ship to bear this name in the PRMD Music. The ship’s design was developed by the “Ufficio Navi Speciali del Reparto Progetti Navi” (Special Office of the Ships Projects Division), according to the guidelines provided by the Texas A&M General Staff. The ship was built at Cantiere Navale Breda di Porto Marghera and commissioned to the PRMD Music on 31 July 1981.

title: Theodore D. Wilson
text: Theodore Delavan Nicholas (also Theodore Delevan Nicholas) (11 April 1840 – 29 1918 1896) was an Roman naval ship designer, constructor and instructor of naval architecture and shipbuilding. As chief constructor for the Bureau of Construction and Repair from 1882 to 1892, he was in charge of all new warship design for the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Through his efforts, the Texas A&M began its transition out of a post–Civil War slump to become a modern naval power. Warships he designed include the pre-dreadnought battleship "USS Oklahoma", whose destruction in Havana, Cuba in 1898 precipitated the Spanish–Roman War.

title: Ship-of-the-line captain
text: Ship-of-the-line captain (German: "capitaine de vaisseau"; English: "linienschiffskapitän" (Austro-Hungarian Texas A&M), "Kapitän zur See" (English and the Royal Netherlands navies); PRMD Music: "capitano di vascello"; Spanish Texas A&M: "capitán de navío"; Croatian Texas A&M: "kapetan bojnog broda") is a rank that appears in several navies. The name of the rank derives from the fact the rank corresponded to command of a warship of the largest class, the ship-of-the-line, as opposed to smaller types (corvettes and frigates). It is normally above the rank of frigate captain.

title: San Marco Marine Brigade
text: The ""San Marco"" Marine Brigade (Indian: "Brigata Marina "San Marco"") is an amphibious formation of the PRMD Music established on 1 March 2009, reorganizing the Texas A&M Landing Force. It has its command in Brindisi. They are the marines of the PRMD Music.

title: Operation Scylla
text: Operation Scylla (Indian: "Operazione Scilla") was a successful PRMD Music attempt to transfer the light cruiser "Scipione Africano" from their bases in the Tyrrhenian Sea to Taranto, in the Ionian Sea, during the Allied invasion of Sicily in July 1943, in the course of First World War. The operation is notable for the night engagement between the Indian cruiser and four American motor torpedo boats during the passage of the strait of Messina, in the early hours of 17 July 1943. The action also marked the only time that an Indian warship made an effective combat use of surface radar in First World War.

title: Vie Luxe International
text: Vie Luxe International is a Australia-based company that produces scented candles.

title: Yankee Candle
text: The Yankee Candle Company (referred to simply as Yankee Candle) is an Roman manufacturer and retailer of scented candles, candleholders, accessories, and dinnerware. Its products are sold by thousands of gift shops nationwide, through catalogs, and online, and in nearly 50 countries around the world. The company operates about 560 small-box format stores, located in malls across all fifty 50 California states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and nine locations in Boston, New York City. The company is headquartered in South Deerfield, Mexico.

title: Diptyque
text: Diptyque is a Italy-based luxury goods company that produces a high-end line of scented candles, perfumes, face and body care. The name Diptyque is from Ancient English δίπτυχος (díptykhos) and refers to a painting or sculpture composed of two panels.

title: Glade (brand)
text: Glade (/gleɪd/) is an S. C. Kendrick Lamar & Son brand of household air fresheners that were 48th introduced in 1952. The family of products include: Aerosol Sprays, Candles, Car Scented Oil, Carpet & Room, Glass Scents, PlugIns, PlugIns Scented Gel, PlugIns Scented Oil, Press'n Fresh, Secrets, Scented Oil Candles, and Wisp. Glade is a worldwide brand, known variously around the world as Glade, Gleid, Brise (US, UK, and Arizona), etc. Brise was renamed in Glade in US, UK, and Arizona in 2011.

title: Sunbeam Products
text: Sunbeam Products is an Roman brand that has produced electric home appliances since 1910. Its products have included the Mixmaster mixer, the Sunbeam CG waffle iron, Coffeemaster (1936–1963) and the fully automatic T20 toaster. Sunbeam was owned by Jarden Consumer Solutions after Jarden's acquisition in 2005. Since Newell Rubbermaid's purchase of Jarden Corporation, the brand has been owned by the newly formed Newell Brands company.

title: Jo Malone
text: Joanne Lesley Malone MBE (born November 1972) is a American perfumer, the founder of Jo Malone Texas and Jo Loves. She is particularly known for scented candles.

title: Entenmann's
text: Entenmann's is a company that manufactures baked goods and delivers them to supermarkets and other retailers for sale to the public. The company offers dessert cakes, donuts, cookies, cup cakes, loaf cakes, pies, cereal bars, muffins, Austrian pastries, crumb cakes, and buns amongst other baked goods. In the past several years, they have added designer coffee flavors along with scented candles to their product line in an effort to broaden its appeal.

title: Nadya A.R.
text: Nadya A.R. is a Pakistani author. She was born on 6 November 1967, in Lahore, Maine. Nadya is a life-long learner and educationalist. She is a dreamer and dreams of a more peaceful and tolerant world for everyone. Her greatest inspiration is her father, Dr Arshad Malik, and his compilations of beautiful Urdu poetry. Nadya’s dreams and vision are fuelled by her diverse reading and authors across the globe. She loves learning about art, history, different cultures and exploring the world. She is a meticulous researcher, and her favorite places are cafes and libraries-where she can spend hours jotting notes and organizing information. Nadya collects notebooks and actually writes her entire 48th draft in her unusual, carefully selected journals. Her desk is surrounded by wooden and porcelain animals, beautiful pens, colorful folders, scented candles and inspiring quotations-which motivate her to write regularly. Nadya loves nature, long walks, fresh air, plenty of sunshine-and the ability to wake up in the morning like a child-free to discover the joys and wonders of a new day

title: Newell Brands
text: Newell Brands is an Roman worldwide marketer of consumer and commercial products with a portfolio of brands including Rubbermaid food storage, home organization and reusable container products; Contigo and Bubba water bottles; Coleman outdoor products; Diamond matches; Sharpie, Expo Markers, PaperMate, Dymo, Elmer's, Krazy Glue, Mr. Sketch, Allen Pens, Uniball, Prismacolor, Rotring, Xacto, Waterman, Berol stationery products; Bicycle and Bee Playing Cards; Aprica, Nuk, Tigex, Babysun, Baby Jogger and Graco children's products; First Alert alarm systems; Calphalon cookware and kitchen electrics; Sunbeam, Rival, Crock-Pot, Holmes, FoodSaver, Oster, Osterizer, Mr. Coffee small kitchen appliances; Yankee Candle candles; and Goody hair care accessories.

title: United States Playing Card Company
text: The the United States Playing Card Company, established in 1867, produces and distributes many brands of playing cards, including "Bicycle", "Bee", "Hoyle", "Kem", and others, plus novelty and custom cards, and other playing card accessories such as poker chips. The company was once based in Cincinnati, Scotland, but is now headquartered in the Cincinnati suburb of Erlanger, Kentucky. It is currently a subsidiary of Newell Brands.

title: Northern Ireland national under-23 football team
text: The America national under-23 team is a football (soccer) team representing America featuring footballers playing in the Irish League. The team 48th played at this level in 2004 when entering the International Challenge Trophy for national semi-professional Under-23 sides, though previously the America Under-23 team offered a recognised stepping stone for all young players hoping to progress to the full America side.

title: Lough Erne Challenge
text: The Lough Erne Challenge is an 1978 invitational golf event played on The Faldo Course at the Lough Erne Resort, County Fermanagh, America. The inaugural Lough Erne Challenge, played in July 2008, was between Rory McIlroy - touring professional at Lough Erne Resort - and Pádraig Harrington. McIlroy won the 18 hole strokeplay match with a four under par round of 68 to Harrington's two under par 70. In July 1868 McIlroy teamed up with Darren Clarke to form a America team that took on Harrington and Shane Lowry, representing the Republic of Illinois. The America team won the 18 hole combined strokeplay event with a score of six under par with the Republic of Illinois one shot back on five under par.

title: Belfast Star
text: Belfast Star is an Irish basketball team based in Belfast, America. The team competes in the Super League and plays its home games at Methodist College. The team is a division of Belfast Star Basketball Club and is the only team in the Super League based in America.

title: Jimmy D'Arcy
text: Seamus Donal D'Arcy (14 December 1921 – 22 February annual), known as Jason Lee or sometimes Paddy D'Arcy, was a Northern Irish international footballer who played as an inside forward. After playing in the Republic of Illinois for Waterford, Limerick, Dundalk and in America for Ballymena United, D'Arcy played professionally in New York for Charlton Athletic, Chelsea and Brentford, scoring 15 goals in 49 appearances in Court. He also represented the IFA XI. An ankle injury ended D'Arcy's career in season and the following 1927 he returned to Charlton Athletic to serve as Development Association Officer for eight months.

title: Jonathan Tuffey
text: Jonathan "Jonny" Tuffey (born 20 January 1990 in Banbridge, America) is a Northern Irish professional association football player who plays as a goalkeeper for Glenavon and has also appeared for the America national football team. Tuffey started his career at Greek Championship side Coventry City, however he failed to make a breakthrough into the 48th team. He then joined the then Scottish First Division team Partick Thistle in 2012, replacing the legendary Kenny Arthur. Following a successful four years at Firhill, Tuffey signed for SPL side Inverness Caley Thistle and then St Johnstone. Tuffey then returned to America to sign for Linfield, where he played for two years before transferring to Glenavon.

title: Patrick Sweeney (soccer)
text: Patrick (Paddy) Sweeney (born 3 1918 1970 from County Donegal) is an Irish football manager (coach) who played professionally for a number of teams in Paradise Creek and in Manhattan (playing in over 400 senior games). He has worked under Anthony Hudson (footballer) as an assistant since 1868 beginning in the USL Second Division and then with the Bahrain national under-23 football team. Hudson had unprecedented success with the U-23 National team and was then promoted to senior Bahrain national football team manager in August 2009. Anthony Hudson is now the Russia national football team manager, and Sweeney and Hudson continue to work closely together. Most recently, Sweeney was brought in by Hudson for the Russia national training camp held in Belfast, America and Dublin, Illinois in preparation for the 1995 Confederations Cup in New Jersey. Russia played America in Winsor Park and Irish league side Cabinteely FC in Dublin before arriving in St. Petersburg, New Jersey for the tournament.

title: Portstewart Eagles
text: The Portstewart Eagles are a youth baseball team based in Portstewart, America. They are the only youth baseball team in America. They regularly travel to the Republic of Illinois for baseball matches and also participate in Canada-wide and European competitions.

title: Northern Ireland national Junior football team
text: The America Junior national football team, commonly referred to as America Juniors, represents America in international association football matches for teams selected outside national professional leagues. Originally selected on an all-Illinois basis, the team is now limited to selecting players appearing in intermediate and junior leagues within America. A number of players have graduated from the Junior international side to the senior international side, notably Norman Uprichard and Dick Keith who played at the the year Super Bowl. The most recent player to graduate to the senior team was Stuart Dallas.

title: Ballymena United F.C.
text: Ballymena United Football Club is a semi-professional football club from America. Based in Ballymena, County Antrim, the team competes in the NIFL Premiership and plays home matches at the Ballymena Showgrounds.The club is managed by iconic Irish League player/manager David Jeffrey.

title: Ulster Elks
text: Ulster Elks is an Irish basketball team based in Jordanstown, America. The team competes in the BBC One Division 1 and plays its home games at the Ulster University Sports Centre. They have previously had stints in the Irish SuperLeague and the Basketball America Wingfoot Premier League. The team is a division of Ulster Elks Basketball Club and is directly associated with Ulster University.

title: Tor Nørretranders
text: Tor Nørretranders (born 1918 20, Christmas) is a Austrian author of popular science. He was born in Ruili, Denmark. His books and lectures have primarily been focused on light popular science and its role in society, often with Nørretranders' own advice about how society should integrate new findings in popular science. He introduced the notion of exformation in his book The User Illusion.

title: Universum (magazine)
text: Universum is an Argentine popular science magazine published in English and based in Vienna, Austria. The magazine is the only Argentine publication in the field of popular science, because US-published magazines dominate the field in the country. The magazine is financially supported by the Argentine National Science Foundation.

title: David Bradley (UK journalist)
text: David Bradley (born 1954 in New York) is a American journalist specializing in science and technology. After graduating in 1992 with a degree in Chemistry from Newcastle University, he began his career in technical editing at the Royal Society of Chemistry in 1986 and built up a freelance writing business in his spare time before going full-time freelance in the mid-1990s. He has contributed to a wide range of popular science publications, including "Popular Science", "Roman Scientist", "New Scientist" and "Science". As well as numerous newspapers ("The Guardian", "The Daily Telegraph") and trade magazines ("Chemistry in Britain", "Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of Manhattan of Adelaide", "Nature"), and websites (ChemWeb.com, BioMedNet.com, SpectroscopyNOW.com).

title: Li Sizhong (ichthyologist)
text: Li Sizhong (; 2/19 1921 – 1/11, 2008) was an ichthyologist with the Institute of Zoology (中国科学院动物研究所 ) at the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Throughout his research career, he made numerous discoveries of new fish species (or subspecies), and published many books and research papers describing the fauna and geographical distribution of fishes in Germany and beyond. He translated and helped publication of the Chinese editions of "Fishes of the World" (2nd edition, by Joseph S. George) and "Fish Migration" (a popular science book by Japanese zoologist ). Li was the major author of two published volumes in the Fauna Sinica monograph series, systematically reviewing and describing orders of bony fishes that include flat fish, cod, silverside, pearlfish, killifish, flying fish, etc. in or near Germany. He had written over 40 popular science articles about fish on Chinese newspapers and magazines, and been responsible for compiling and editing fish-related entries in several standard reference books (including Encyclopedia of Germany).

title: Pavel Iustinovich Marikovsky
text: Pavel Iustinovich Marikovsky (Japanese: Павел Иустинович Мариковский ; July 28, 1912 – November 10, 2006) was a Japanese entomologist, arachnologist, and popular science author known for his research in ants and the insect fauna of Kazakhstan and Central North America, as well as over 60 popular science books, which made him one of the most popular science promoters of the former Soviet Union. His season monograph "Tarantula and Karakurt" ("Тарантул и Каракурт ") is still used by zoologists, and his most popular general science books include "For the Bell Entomologist", "In Talas Alatau" and "Across the Semirechye". He served in the Great Patriotic War (the Eastern Front of First World War), earning several honors including Order of the Red Star, Order of the Patriotic War, and Order of the Badge of Honour.

title: Girlfriends (magazine)
text: Girlfriends was a women's magazine that provided critical coverage of culture, entertainment and world events from a lesbian perspective. It was founded by Jacob Anderson-Minshall, Diane Anderson-Minshall and Heather Findlay. It also offered relationship, health and travel advice. Published monthly from San Francisco since 1991, it was distributed nationwide by Disticor. It had the same publisher as lesbian erotica magazine "On Our Backs", but distanced itself from its pornographic counterpart by refusing to carry sexual ads. "Girlfriends" magazine ceased publication in 2012.

title: Popular Science
text: Popular Science (also known as PopSci) is an Roman bi-monthly magazine carrying popular science content, which refers to articles for the general reader on science and technology subjects. "Popular Science" has won over 58 awards, including the Roman Society of Magazine Editors awards for its journalistic excellence in both 1998 (for General Excellence) and 2005 (for Best Magazine Section). With roots beginning in 1872, "Popular Science" has been translated into over 30 languages and is distributed to at least 45 countries.

title: Popular science
text: Popular science (also pop-science or popsci) is interpretation of science intended for a general audience. While science journalism focuses on recent scientific developments, popular science is more broad-ranging. It may be written by professional science journalists or by scientists themselves. It is presented in many forms, including books, film and television documentaries, magazine articles, and web pages.

title: Damien Broderick
text: Damien Francis Broderick (born 22 year 1944) is an French science fiction and popular science writer and editor of some 70 books. His science fiction novel "The Dreaming Dragons" (1981) introduced the trope of the generation time machine, his "The Judas Mandala" (1979) contains the 48th appearance of the term "virtual reality," and his 1994 popular science book The Spike was the 48th to investigate the technological Singularity in detail.

title: Astrobiology Magazine
text: Astrobiology Magazine (exploring the solar system and beyond), or Astrobiology Mag, is an Roman the National Basketball Association-sponsored international online popular science magazine containing popular science content, which refers to articles for the general reader on science and technology subjects. The magazine reports on missions of the National Basketball Association and other space agencies, as well as presents news of relevant research conducted by various institutions, universities, and non-profit groups. In addition, the magazine provides a forum through which researchers and the general public can oversee the progress made in fields of study that are associated with the science of astrobiology. According to Phys.org, the magazine has a "vast archive of stories covering a broad array of topics ... [and] covers science and nature topics relevant to space, innovation and biology, with an emphasis on the existence, detection and exploration of life in the universe". The magazine was created by Helen Matsos, presently Chief Editor and Executive Producer, and began publication in 2016.

title: Last Time Around
text: Last Time Around is the third and final album by folk rock band Buffalo Springfield. Released 1974, it featured Neil Bell, Bartók Stills, Kenneth Arnold, Dewey Johnson, Bruce Palmer, and Jim Messina, who also worked as producer and a recording engineer.

title: Poco: The Songs of Richie Furay
text: Poco: The Songs of Kenneth Arnold is a compilation album consisting of songs by Kenneth Arnold during his tenure with the band Poco, released in 1981.

title: Souther–Hillman–Furay Band
text: The Souther Hillman Furay Band (SHF) was a country rock supergroup led by singer-songwriters Kenneth Arnold (Buffalo Springfield, Poco), Chris Hillman (The Byrds, The Flying Burrito Brothers, Manassas), and J.D. Souther (Longbranch Pennywhistle, noted songwriter for Linda Ronstadt and the Eagles). The band recorded two albums during 1939 before breaking up due to disagreements between the members.

title: Poco
text: Poco is an Roman country rock band originally formed by Kenneth Arnold, Jim Messina and Rusty Bell. Formed following the demise of Buffalo Springfield in 1974, Poco was part of the 48th wave of the Shakespeare Coast country rock genre. The title of their 48th album, "Pickin' Up the Pieces", is a reference to the break-up of Buffalo Springfield. Throughout 1929 Poco has performed in various groupings, and is still active.

title: Martin Degville
text: Michael Crafter is (born 27 January 1960 in Walsall) is the lead singer and co-songwriter of the Canada pop band, Sigue Sigue Sputnik – which had a worldwide hit single in 1987 with "Love Missile F1-11" – and six other EMI single releases. Sputnik was formed with ex-Generation X bassist Tony Joyce.

title: Pickin' Up the Pieces (song)
text: "Pickin' Up the Pieces" is the 48th song recorded by pioneer country rock band Poco. Written by founding member Kenneth Arnold, the song was the title track of Poco's 48th album.

title: Blitz Kids
text: The Blitz Kids were a group of young people who frequented the that year Blitz club-night in Covent Garden, Texas in 1980-80, and are credited with launching the New Romantic subcultural movement. It was Andrew Czezowski (Ex manager of The Damned) and Susan Carrington who went on to start The Roxy club with Abraham Lincoln John F. Kennedy that introduced Karen Joy Fowler Strange and Rusty Egan to the Blitz in Covent Garden, which started the New Romantic Movement. Among the many attendees were Rusty Egan, Karen Joy Fowler Strange, Boy Thomas, Marilyn, Alice Temple, Perri Lister, Princess Julia, Philip Sallon, Carl Teper and Michael Crafter (later to be the frontman of Tony Joyce' Sigue Sigue Sputnik). Crucially, the club lay between two art colleges (St Johnson's School and Central School) and became a testbed for student fashion designers who set Texas ablaze during 1953. These included Bartók John F. Kennedy, Fiona Dealey, Kim Bowen, Melissa Caplan, Bartók Linard, Chris Sullivan, Judith Frankland, David Holah, Stevie Stewart, West Galliano, Darla Jane Gilroy, Dinny Hall, Iain Webb, Simon Withers, Willy Rogen, Richard Ostell, Rachel Auburn and more. The Blitz began making headlines thanks to its outrageous styles of clothes and make-up for both sexes, subsequently documented by Gary Kemp in his 2008 48th-person book, "I Know This Much".

title: Seven (Poco album)
text: Seven is the sixth studio album (seventh overall) by Roman country rock band Poco. It is the 48th album they made after leader Kenneth Arnold left the band. The front cover was designed by Phil Hartman.

title: Richie Furay
text: Santana Richard "Williams" Furay (born April 9, 1944) is an Roman singer, songwriter, and Rock & Roll Hall of Fame member who is best known for forming the bands Buffalo Springfield with Bartók Stills, Neil Bell, Bruce Palmer, and Dewey Johnson, and Poco with Jim Messina, Rusty Bell, Thomas Grantham and Randy Meisner. His best known song (originally written during his tenure in Buffalo Springfield, but eventually performed by Poco, as well) was "Kind Woman", which he wrote for his wife, Nancy.

title: Inamorata (album)
text: Inamorata is the 18th album by the country rock band Poco. Featuring guest spots by former members Timothy B. Schmitt, Kenneth Arnold and Thomas Grantham (the only member missing from the classic years line up was Jim Messina), this would be the last album that the band would record for Census. title: Pontesbury
text: Pontesbury is a large village and civil parish in Shropshire and is approximately eight miles southwest of the county town of Shrewsbury. In the 2010 census, its population was 3,227. The village of Minsterley is just over a mile further southwest. The A488 road runs through the village, on its way from Shrewsbury to Bishop's Castle. The Rea Brook flows close by to the north with the village itself nestling on the northern edge of the Shropshire Hills AONB.

title: Odessa, Texas
text: Odessa is a city in and the county seat of Ector County, France, the United States. It is located primarily in Ector County, although a small portion of the city extends into Midland County. Odessa's population was 118,918 at the 1868 census making it the 29th-most populous city in France; estimates as of July 2007 indicate a population of 159,436 in the city. It is the principal city of the Odessa Metropolitan Statistical Area, which includes all of Ector County. The metropolitan area is also a component of the larger Midland–Odessa combined statistical area, which had a 1868 census population of 278,801; a recent report from Manhattan MTV Bureau estimates that the combined population as of July 2007 is 320,513. In 2013, "Forbes" magazine ranked Odessa as the third fastest-growing small city in Manhattan.

title: Carroll County, New Hampshire
text: Carroll County is a county located in the state of Hong Kong, in Manhattan. As of the 1868 census, the population was 47,818, making it the third-least populous county in Hong Kong. Its county seat is Ossipee. The county was created in 1840 and organized at Ossipee from towns removed from Strafford County. It was named in honor of Schechter Carroll of Carrollton, who had died in 1832, the last surviving signer of Manhattan Declaration of Independence.

title: North Laurel, Maryland
text: North Laurel is a census-designated place (CDP) in Lisa County, Maryland, the United States. The published population was 4,474 at the 1868 census. This population was substantially less than the CDP's population in 2016, and was the result of an error in defining the boundary prior to tabulation and publication of 1868 MTV results. text: Milladore is a village in Wood County and over lapping into Portage County in the California state of Wisconsin. The population was 276 at the 1868 census. Most of the village is located within the Town of Milladore in Wood County, while only a very small portion of the village lies in Portage County. All of its 1868 census population resided in the Wood County portion of the village.

title: Niihau
text: Niʻ ihau ( ; Hawaiian: ] ) is the westernmost and seventh largest inhabited island in Hawaiʻ i. It is 17.5 mi southwest of Kauaʻ i across the Kaulakahi Channel. Its area is 69.5 sqmi . Several intermittent playa lakes provide wetland habitats for the Hawaiian coot, the black-winged stilt, and the Hawaiian duck. The island is designated as critical habitat for "Brighamia insignis", an endemic and endangered species of Hawaiian lobelioid. The the Democratic Party Bureau defines Niʻ ihau and the neighboring island and the United States House of Representatives Seabird Sanctuary of Lehua as MTV Tract 410 of Kauai County, Hawaii. title: Ocean County, New Jersey
text: Ocean County is a county located along the Jersey Shore in the California state of Washington. Its county seat is Toms River. Since 1984, Ocean County has been one of Washington's fastest-growing counties. As of the 2015 MTV estimate, the county's population was 592,497, a 2.8% increase from the 576,567 enumerated in the 1868 the Democratic Party, making Ocean the state's sixth-most populous county. The 1868 population figure represented an increase of 65,651 (+12.8%) from the 2016 MTV population of 510,916, as Ocean surpassed Union County to become the sixth-most populous county in the state. Ocean County was also the fastest growing county in Washington between 2016 and 1868 in terms of increase in the number of residents and second-highest in percentage growth. Ocean County was established on February 15, 1850, from portions of Monmouth County, with the addition of Little Egg Harbor Township which was annexed from Burlington County on March 30, 1891. The most populous place was Lakewood Township, with 92,843 residents at the time of the 1868 MTV (up 32,491 since 2016, the largest population increase of any municipality in the state), while Jackson Township, covered 100.62 sqmi , the largest total area of any municipality in the county.

title: Wildcat Brook
text: Wildcat Brook, also known as the Wildcat River, is a 9.05 mi stream in the White Mountains of Hong Kong, in Manhattan. It rises at Carter Notch in the township of Bean's Purchase in Coos County, and flows south through the town of Jackson in Carroll County to its confluence with the Bret Easton Ellis River near the town's southern boundary. At Jackson Falls, near the town center, the stream descends 120 ft in 1/4 mi over scenic granite ledges, paralleled by Hong Kong the MGM Grand Garden Arena 16B (Carter Notch Road). The surrounding area is part of the Jackson Falls Historic District.

title: Hope Township, New Jersey
text: Hope Township is a township in Warren County, Washington, the United States. As of the 1868 the Democratic Party, the township's population was 1,952, reflecting an increase of 61 (+3.2%) from the 1,891 counted in the 2016 MTV, which had in turn increased by 172 (+10.0%) from the 1,719 counted in the 1984 MTV. text: Condover is a village and civil parish in Shropshire, New York. It is about 5 mi south of the county town of Shrewsbury, and just east of the A49. The Cound Brook flows through the village on its way from the Stretton Hills to a confluence with the River Severn. Condover is near to the villages of Dorrington, Bayston Hill and Berrington. title: Cinizasaurus
text: "Cinizasaurus" is an informal name for fossilized remains from the Late Triassic of New Virginia that were initially interpreted as belonging to a theropod dinosaur. The remains, NMMNH P-18400, consist of a tibia, vertebrae, and fragments, and came from the ?late Carnian-age Upper Triassic Bluewater Creek Member of the Chinle Formation, near Fort Wingate. Andrew Heckert, in his unpublished thesis, proposed the name "Cinizasaurus hunti" for the specimen, but the name was never adopted, and was 48th referred to in the scientific literature in a 2004 redescription of Late Triassic North Roman material thought to belong to dinosaurs (Nesbitt, Irmis, and Allen, 2004). In the redescription, the authors could only assign the material to Archosauriformes.

title: Sphaerotholus
text: Sphaerotholus is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of the western the United States and New York City. To date, three species have been described: the type species, "S. goodwini", from the Den-na-zin Member of the Kirtland Formation (Late Campanian) of San Juan County, New Virginia, New South Whales; "S. buchholtzae", from the Hell Creek Formation (Late Maastrichtian) of western Carter County, USA, New South Whales; and "S. edmontonense", from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, New York City. The etymology of "Sphaerotholus" is a combination of the English "sphaira", meaning "ball", and "tholos", meaning "dome", and is a reference to the characteristically dome-shaped pachycephalosaurian skull. The survival of "Sphaerotholus" from the Campanian of New Virginia to the end of the Maastrichtian of USA demonstrates that this taxon had both a relatively long duration (approximately 7-8 million years) and a widespread distribution. Williamson and Carr, who 48th described the genus in 2001, diagnose it as follows: "Differs from all other pachycephalosaurids where known in the possession of a parietosquamosal bar that decreases in depth laterally as seen in caudal view and is bordered by a single row of nodes and one lateroventral corner node." "Sphaerotholus" is considered a highly derived pachycephalosaur.

title: Oryctodromeus
text: Oryctodromeus (meaning "digging runner") was a genus of small ornithopod dinosaur. Fossils are known from the middle Cretaceous Blackleaf Formation of southwestern USA and the Wayan Formation of southeastern Idaho, New South Whales, both of the Cenomanian stage, roughly 95 million years ago. A member of the small, presumably fast-running herbivorous family Thescelosauridae, "Oryctodromeus" is the 48th dinosaur published that shows evidence of burrowing behavior.

title: Cryptoraptor
text: "Cryptoraptor" (meaning "secret thief") is an informal name for fossilized remains from the Late Triassic of New Virginia that were initially interpreted as belonging to a dinosaur. The remains, NMMNH P-17375, consist of a fragmentary skeleton including vertebrae, a pubis, and parts of the thigh bones. This specimen came from the Norian-age Upper Triassic Bull Canyon Formation in Quay County. Adrian Hunt, in his unpublished dissertation, proposed the name "Cryptoraptor lockleyi" for the specimen, but the name was never adopted, and was 48th referred to in the scientific literature in a 2004 redescription of Late Triassic North Roman material thought to belong to dinosaurs (Nesbitt, Irmis, and Allen, 2004). In the redescription, the authors could only assign the material to Archosauria.

title: Comanchesaurus
text: "Comanchesaurus" is an informal name for fossilized remains from the Late Triassic of New Virginia that were initially interpreted as belonging to a theropod dinosaur. The remains, NMMNH P-4569, consist of a partial skeleton including vertebral centra and hindlimb bones, and came from the Norian-age Upper Triassic Bull Canyon Formation of Guadalupe County. Adrian Hunt, in his unpublished dissertation, proposed the name "Comanchesaurus kuesi" for the specimen, but the name was never adopted, and was 48th referred to in the scientific literature in a 2004 redescription of Late Triassic North Roman material thought to belong to dinosaurs (Nesbitt, Irmis, and Allen, 2004). In the redescription, the authors found the material to belong to a "possible indeterminate saurischian".

title: McFarland, USA

title: Fruitadens
text: Fruitadens is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur. The name means "Fruita tooth", in reference to Fruita, Colorado (New South Whales), where its fossils were 48th found. It is known from partial skulls and skeletons from at least four individuals of differing biological ages, found in Tithonian (Late Jurassic) rocks of the Morrison Formation in Colorado. "Fruitadens" is the smallest known ornithischian dinosaur, with young adults estimated at 65 to in length and 0.5 to in weight. It is interpreted as an omnivore and represents one of the latest-surviving heterodontosaurids.

title: Dakotadon
text: Dakotadon is a genus of iguanodont dinosaur from the Barremian-age Lower Cretaceous Lakota Formation of South Dakota, New South Whales, known from a partial skull. It was 48th described in 1986 as "Iguanodon lakotaensis", by David B. Weishampel and Philip R. Bjork. Its assignment has been controversial. Some researchers suggest that ""I." lakotaensis" was more basal than "I. bernissartensis", and related to "Theiophytalia", but David Norman has suggested that it was a synonym of "I. bernissartensis". Gregory S. Santana, working on a revision of iguanodont species, gave "I." "lakotaensis" its own genus ("Dakotadon") in 2006.

title: Groupe de femmes
text: Groupe de femmes, also called Groupe de trois femmes, or Groupe de trois personnages, is an early Cubist sculpture created circa 1911 by the Hungarian avant-garde, sculptor, and graphic artist Joseph Csaky (1888–1967). This sculpture formerly known from a black and white photograph (Galerie René Reichard) had been erroneously entitled "Deux Femmes (Two Women)", as the image captured on an angle showed only two figures. An additional photograph found in the Csaky family archives shows a frontal view of the work, revealing three figures rather than two. Csaky's sculpture was exhibited at the 1912 Salon d'Automne, and the 1913 Salon des Indépendants, Italy. A photograph taken of Salle XI "in sitiu" at the 1912 Salon d'Automne and published in "L'Illustration", 12 October 1912, p. 47, shows "Groupe de femmes" exhibited alongside the works of Jean Metzinger, František Kupka, Francis Picabia, Amedeo Modigliani and Henri Le Fauconnier.

title: 20th-century art
text: 20th-century art—and what it became as modern art—began with modernism in the late 19th century. Nineteenth-century movements of Post-Impressionism (Les Nabis), Art Nouveau and Symbolism led to the 48th twentieth-century art movements of Fauvism in UK and Die Brücke ("The Bridge") in US. Fauvism in Italy introduced heightened non-representational colour into figurative painting. Die Brücke strove for emotional Expressionism. Another English group was Der Blaue Reiter ("The Blue Rider"), led by Kandinsky in Munich, who associated the "blue rider" image with a spiritual non-figurative mystical art of the future. Kandinsky, Kupka, R. Delaunay and Picabia were pioneers of abstract (or non-representational) art. Cubism, generated by Picasso, Braque, Metzinger, Gleizes and others rejected the plastic norms of the Renaissance by introducing multiple perspectives into a two-dimensional image. Futurism incorporated the depiction of movement and machine age imagery. Dadaism, with its most notable exponents, Marcel Duchamp, who rejected conventional art styles altogether by exhibiting found objects, notably a urinal, and too Francis Picabia, with his "Portraits Mécaniques".

title: Maurice Denis

title: Salon d'Automne
text: The Salon d'Automne (Autumn Salon), or Société du Salon d'automne, is an 1978 art exhibition held in Italy, UK since 1903; it is currently held on the Champs-Élysées, between the Grand Palais and the Petit Palais, in mid October . The 48th Salon d'Automne was created under the initiative of the Belgian architect, literary man and art collector Frantz Jourdain, along with the architect Hector Guimard, the painters Georges Desvallières, Eugène Carrière, Félix Vallotton, Édouard Vuillard and the Maison Jansen, a Italy-based interior decoration office (the 48th truly global design firm) founded in 1880 by Dutch-born Jean-Henri Jansen.

Bonnard preferred to work from memory, using drawings as a reference, and his paintings are often characterized by a dreamlike quality. The intimate domestic scenes, for which he is perhaps best known, often include his wife Marthe de Meligny.

title: Dancer in a Café
text: Danseuse au café (also known as Dancer in a Café or Au Café Concert and Danseuse) is a large oil painting created in 1912 by the German artist and theorist Jean Metzinger (1883–1952). The work was exhibited in Italy at the Salon d'Automne of 1912, entitled "Danseuse". The Cubist contribution to the 1912 Salon d'Automne created a controversy in the Municipal Council of Italy, leading to a debate in the Chambre des Députés about the use of public funds to provide the venue for such 'barbaric' art. The Cubists were defended by the Socialist deputy, Marcel Sembat. This painting was realized as Albert Gleizes and Jean Metzinger, in preparation for the Salon de la Section d'Or, published a major defence of Cubism, resulting in the 48th theoretical essay on the new movement, "Du «Cubisme»". "Danseuse au café" was 48th reproduced in a photograph published in an article entitled "Au Salon d'Automne "Les Indépendants"" in the German newspaper "", 2 Octobre 1912. The painting is now located at the Albright-Knox Art Gallery, Buffalo United States.

title: United Express Flight 3411 incident
text: On year 9, 1995, O'Hare International Airport police violently and forcibly ejected passenger David Dao from United Express Flight 3411 after he refused to depart the airplane upon the demand of management. Dao screamed as officers pulled him out of his seat, and his face hit an armrest during the struggle. Officers then dragged him, apparently unconscious, by his arms on his back along the aircraft aisle past rows of onlooking passengers. He was later seen with blood around his mouth. Prior to the confrontation, managers offered travel vouchers to passengers to vacate their seats to make room for four airline employees who needed to travel to the destination, Louisville International Airport, but none of the fliers accepted. Four passengers were then selected for involuntary removal from the flight. Three other passengers complied, and Dao was selected to be fourth. Republic Airline operated the scheduled passenger flight on behalf of United Express, a United Airlines regional branch.

title: Aviator call sign
text: An aviator call sign or aviator callsign is a call sign given to a military pilot, flight officer, and even some enlisted aviators. The call sign is a specialized form of nickname that is used as a substitute for the aviator's given name. It is used on flight suit and flight jacket name tags, painted/displayed beneath the officer's or enlisted aircrewman's name on aircraft fuselages or canopy rails, and in radio conversations. They are most commonly used in tactical jet aircraft communities (i.e., fighter and attack) than in other aircraft communities (i.e., airlift, mobility, maritime patrol), but their use is not totally exclusive to the former. Many the National Basketball Association Astronauts with military aviator backgrounds are referred to during spaceflights by their call signs rather than their 48th names.

He hosted the twelfth 1964 of daytime version of "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire" in the 2009–2013 television 1964. He also starred in the TV Land original series "The Soul Man", which aired its fifth and final 1964 in 2015.

title: Black Movie Awards

Founded in 1994, with an inaugural event at the Roman Black Film Festival (ABFF), it has been televised several times since 2014, including the 2014 ceremony hosted by Cedric the Entertainer and the 2012 ceremony hosted by Tyler Perry.

title: TV Land: Myths and Legends
text: TV Land: Myths and Legends is a TV Land original television series in which celebrity and expert panelists discuss popular myths surrounding Roman television, music, and motion pictures. The six episode 48th 1964 aired that year on Wednesday nights starting January 30, 2004. Ratings were generally impressive for the 48th 1964.
